## Common questions

- What is AEO? Answer Engine Optimization means making sure tools like ChatGPT, Google AI and Perplexity can find a business, understand what it does, and recommend it when someone asks for help.
- Is AEO different from SEO? They work together. SEO helps a business rank in a list of links. AEO helps it get named in the answer. AI tools still lean on search results, but they also weigh reviews, what other websites say about the business, and whether its content answers real questions clearly.
- How do AI tools decide who to recommend? They pull from the website, Google Business Profile, reviews, directories, articles and forums. They favour businesses that are clear about what they do, consistent everywhere, and mentioned by sources they trust.
- How long until results show? Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. Google AI and ChatGPT usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why the service starts with 90 days.
- Is a new website needed? No. AudienceIntent works with the existing site: WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Shopify or custom.
- What does the client need to provide? Access to the website and Google Business Profile (or an intro to whoever runs them), plus a monthly progress call.

## What Is Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)? The Complete Guide for 2026

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/what-is-answer-engine-optimization-aeo-the-complete-guide-for-2026
Published: 2026-10-28
Summary: Learn what AEO and GEO mean, how AI chooses businesses to recommend, and how to improve and measure visibility in ChatGPT, Google AI and Perplexity.

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) is the practice of making your business easier to find, understand, cite, and recommend in AI-generated answers. It helps your business appear when people ask ChatGPT, Google AI, or Perplexity questions about what you sell. AEO complements SEO; it does not replace it.

#### TL;DR
- **AEO targets AI answers**, not just search rankings.
- **GEO means Generative Engine Optimization.** For business owners, it describes the same goal under a different name.
- **The foundation is clear content, technical access, real proof, and consistent business information.**
- **Google rankings do not guarantee AI recommendations.** Track both.
- **Measure mentions, citations, competitor share of voice, and business results.** No provider can guarantee inclusion in a specific answer.

#### Why AEO Matters in 2026

AEO matters because customers can now ask for a recommendation without opening a traditional search results page. Your business needs to be understandable both to search engines and to the systems that write those answers.

According to [OpenAI figures reported by Big Technology in November 2026](https://www.bigtechnology.com/p/openai-chatgpt-search-is-about-20), ChatGPT has about **1.2 billion weekly active users**. OpenAI also says ChatGPT's search volume is about **20% of Google's**. Those figures describe platform use, not the number of people searching for your particular service.

Google remains enormous. It processes **more than 5 trillion searches a year**, roughly **14 billion a day**, according to [Google's 2025 figures reported by Search Engine Land](https://searchengineland.com/google-5-trillion-searches-per-year-452928).

The practical change is not that Google has disappeared. It is that buyers have another way to choose. A customer can ask, “Which company should I hire for this job?” and receive a shortlist with explanations instead of a list of pages.

AEO helps your business become a credible option in that answer. Being mentioned can matter even when the customer does not immediately click through to your website.

#### What Is GEO?

**GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization. It has the same business goal as AEO: helping your business get mentioned, cited, and recommended in AI-generated answers.** You do not need separate strategies just because providers use different names.

Historically, AEO also described work aimed at featured snippets, direct-answer boxes, and voice assistants. GEO emphasizes answers that generative AI systems assemble from multiple sources. Today, the terms overlap heavily.

The [November 2023 GEO research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) studied ways to improve source visibility in generative answers. It reported visibility improvements of up to 40% in its experimental setting. That is a research result, not a promise that a business will receive 40% more recommendations or customers.

The useful lesson is to make content worth using as a source. Give direct answers. Support claims with evidence. Attribute outside research. Publish specific information that readers can verify.

Whether you call the work AEO or GEO, the questions remain the same: Does AI understand your business? Does it have trustworthy evidence? Does it name you when the question is relevant?

#### How Does AEO Work?

AEO improves the information AI systems can find and use about your business. It does not give you control over their answers.

Depending on the platform and question, an answer may draw on information learned during training, live web retrieval, search results, or other available sources. Not every response includes a fresh web search.

##### 1. The system interprets the customer's question

The question determines which businesses and sources are relevant. “Who repairs tile roofs in Miami?” asks for a different answer than “How long does a tile roof last?”

Your content should make your services, location, customers, and limits clear enough to match the right questions.

##### 2. It finds information it can access

Accessible pages give retrieval systems something to work with. Blocked pages, inaccessible text, and broken links can prevent useful information from being found.

Technical access is necessary for direct retrieval, but access alone does not earn a recommendation.

##### 3. It selects information relevant to the answer

A specific, supported explanation is more useful than a broad claim such as “We offer the best service.” Clear headings, direct answers, and verifiable facts help a system interpret a page accurately.

##### 4. It generates an answer that may name or cite businesses

Business profiles, reviews, independent coverage, and your own website can all contribute evidence. No public checklist reveals exactly how every platform weighs those sources, and the weighting can change.

#### AEO vs. SEO: What Is the Difference?

SEO helps pages appear in search results. AEO helps information about your business appear inside generated answers. They share much of the same groundwork, but success is measured differently.

| Dimension | SEO | AEO and GEO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main goal | Earn visibility and clicks from search results | Earn relevant mentions, citations, and recommendations |
| Main measures | Rankings, organic traffic, conversions | Answer inclusion, citations, share of voice, referrals |
| Content emphasis | Useful pages matched to search intent | Direct, self-contained answers supported by evidence |
| Shared foundation | Accessible pages, useful content, credible information | Accessible pages, useful content, credible information |

[EMARKETER's explanation of GEO, AEO, and SEO](https://www.emarketer.com/content/faq-on-geo-aeo--where-ai-search-seo-overlap-2026) makes the same central distinction: ranking a page and being selected as a source are different outcomes.

For the full comparison, read [AEO vs. SEO: why they're different and why you need both](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo).

#### The Five Core Pillars of AEO

Useful AEO work combines clear answers, technical access, evidence, consistent business details, and coverage of real customer questions. None of these is a shortcut on its own.

##### 1. Content that answers questions directly

An answer-first page states the useful answer before the background. Each section should make sense when read on its own.

Use descriptive headings, short paragraphs, and concrete details. Put definitions close to the top. Use lists or tables when they make a decision easier.

For example, a service page should explain who the service is for, what it includes, where it is available, and what affects its price. It should not make readers work through several paragraphs before discovering what the business does.

There is no magic paragraph length. The goal is a complete answer, not an arbitrary word count.

##### 2. Technical access

Important content must be accessible to the systems that retrieve it. Check crawler rules, page availability, rendering, internal links, and XML sitemaps.

Different bots serve different purposes:
- **OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot** supports search discovery. **GPTBot** has a separate role related to model training; allowing training is not a requirement for search inclusion.
- **Googlebot** is relevant to Google Search, including AI Overviews and AI Mode.
- **PerplexityBot** supports Perplexity's discovery of web content.

Review the rules for the access you actually want. Do not assume every bot must be allowed.

Keep essential text available without relying entirely on client-side JavaScript. Add accurate structured data where it describes the visible content. An `llms.txt` file is an optional aid, not an established requirement or a guarantee of citations.

##### 3. Evidence people can verify

Specific evidence supports credibility better than self-praise. Show who is behind the business and what supports its claims.

Useful proof includes named authors, relevant qualifications, detailed service explanations, genuine testimonials, and case studies with a clear timeframe. Attribute outside statistics to their original sources when available.

Keep facts current. Update a page when its substance changes rather than changing its date to make old information look new.

##### 4. Consistent business details and outside evidence

Consistent information helps systems identify the same business across different sources. Use the correct business name, address, phone number, services, and locations wherever those details appear.

Independent publications, business profiles, customer reviews, and industry sites may help confirm what your website says. Their importance varies by question, platform, and market.

This does not mean placing your name on as many websites as possible. Relevant, accurate information is more useful than a large collection of weak or misleading listings.

##### 5. Coverage of customer questions

AEO needs to cover questions people ask before they know your business name. Branded searches alone cannot tell you whether new customers are discovering you.

Build content around real decisions: price, suitability, service areas, comparisons, timing, and common problems. Use questions from sales calls, emails, and customer conversations.

Answer those questions honestly. Do not claim to serve a location or offer a service simply to appear for another prompt.

#### Why Local and Service Businesses Have an Opportunity

Local businesses can compete through relevance to a particular place, service, and customer need. Being a large national brand is not a requirement for being a useful recommendation.

Consider the difference between these questions:
- “How does roof repair work?”
- “Who repairs tile roofs in Miami?”
- “Which Miami roofer handles storm damage on tile roofs?”

The later questions require increasingly specific business information. A local provider with accurate service pages, a complete Google Business Profile, and credible proof can be relevant in ways a general article is not.

Explain where you work, what jobs you handle, and what customers should expect. Avoid near-identical location pages that add no local detail.

For a worked example, see [how AI recommendations apply to Miami roofers](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/if-a-miami-homeowner-asks-ai-who-to-call-for-their-roof-will-your-name-come-up).

#### A Practical AEO Starting Checklist

Start by measuring your current visibility, then improve the pages and information closest to customer decisions. You do not need to rebuild your entire website before doing useful work.
1. **Choose real questions.** Write down questions about your services, location, price, and alternatives. Include questions that do not mention your business.
2. **Record a baseline.** Test the same questions across your target platforms. Save the date, wording, answer, named businesses, and source links.
3. **Inspect the cited sources.** Identify which questions your existing pages answer well and where important information is missing.
4. **Improve existing pages first.** Clarify service details, add direct answers, correct outdated facts, and connect related pages with useful internal links.
5. **Resolve access and identity problems.** Check crawler access and correct mismatched business information on major profiles.
6. **Publish missing answers and retest.** Keep a change log so you can compare later results with the work completed.

For a more detailed workflow, use the [step-by-step guide to getting recommended by ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines).

#### How to Measure AEO Performance

Measure whether your business appears in relevant answers, whether those answers cite useful sources, and whether visibility leads to visits or inquiries. Search rankings alone cannot answer those questions.

A mention and a citation are different. A **mention** names your business. A **citation** links to a supporting source. An answer can mention you without linking to your website, or cite your page without recommending your business.

| Metric | What it measures | What to watch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mention rate | Percentage of tracked answers that name your business | Whether inclusion improves for relevant questions |
| Citation rate | Percentage of tracked answers that link to your website | Whether your pages are being used as sources |
| Share of voice | Your share of all monitored business mentions in the same answer set | How visibility compares with tracked competitors |
| Recommendation quality | How accurately and favorably the answer describes your business | Wrong services, locations, or unsupported claims |
| AI referral traffic | Visits attributed to identifiable AI sources | Useful visits, inquiries, and sales where measurable |

Use a consistent prompt set and record the platform, date, and relevant location settings. Repeat checks because one answer is not a stable ranking. Adding easier questions midway through a campaign can make the figures look better without showing real improvement.

In GA4, examine identifiable AI referrals and their outcomes. Attribution is incomplete: some people see an answer and later visit directly or search for your name. Google's AI features are not always separable from other Google traffic in standard reports.

Do not assume AI visitors always convert better. Measure your own inquiries and sales. For more detail, read [how to measure AEO with mentions, citations, share of voice, and business KPIs](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-measure-the-success-of-an-aeo-campaign-metrics-kpis-and-benchmarks-for-2026).

#### How Long Does AEO Take?

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why AudienceIntent's service starts with 90 days.

Finding a page is not the same as recommending the business behind it. Timing depends on the starting website, competition, existing evidence, and questions being tracked.

Use the early period to establish a baseline, resolve access problems, improve important pages, and publish missing answers. Look for repeated patterns over time rather than treating one favorable response as a lasting result.

Nobody can guarantee that your business will appear in a specific AI answer. AudienceIntent promises the work, done properly every month, and an honest report. Read more about [why nobody can guarantee the number-one answer in AI search](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/no-one-can-guarantee-youll-be-the-number-1-answer-in-ai-search-heres-what-actually-works).

Client results show what happened for particular businesses, not what every business should expect. These are different measures and should not be treated as interchangeable:
- **Vault Metal:** AI mentions 169 → 7,808 (+4,520%) and citations 3 → 751 in 90 days.
- **GoldenCrest Metals:** visibility score +202.4% in 90 days.
- **Craft Food Tours:** traffic from AI +312% in 90 days.

See the [Vault Metal case study](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-vault-metal-went-from-invisible-in-ai-to-7-808-mentions-in-90-days) for that example in more detail.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

##### Is SEO still relevant?

Yes. SEO still helps customers find your pages through search results and supports the accessible content that AI systems may use. AEO adds work focused on generated answers. Keep useful SEO work in place rather than replacing it with a new acronym.

##### What makes an AI platform choose one source over another?

Accessibility, relevance, and credible evidence all matter, but platforms do not publish a complete formula for source selection. Make your information easy to retrieve, answer the specific question, and support claims with verifiable facts. No single tactic guarantees selection.

##### Can a business rank well on Google but still be missing from AI answers?

Yes. Strong Google rankings do not guarantee inclusion in an AI-generated answer. The platform may interpret the question differently or select other sources. Test relevant customer questions directly instead of assuming your search rankings describe your AI visibility.

##### Do AI crawlers require a separate setup?

Not always. Many websites are already accessible, but crawler rules, security settings, and JavaScript-dependent content can cause problems. Check the bots relevant to search discovery. OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot serves a different purpose from GPTBot, which relates to model training.

##### How do you measure AEO if there are no fixed rankings?

Track a consistent set of customer questions over time. Record business mentions, source links, competitor appearances, and the accuracy of recommendations. Combine that with identifiable AI referral traffic and inquiries. A single answer or screenshot is not a reliable performance measure.

##### Will AI search reduce traffic to my website?

It can reduce clicks for questions answered fully inside the interface. It can also send visitors who want to investigate a recommendation. Neither a net traffic gain nor a higher conversion rate is guaranteed. Measure visits, inquiries, and sales for your own business.

##### What is the right first step for a business that wants to appear in AI search?

Establish a baseline before buying services or rewriting your site. Check whether AI names your business or competitors for real customer questions, then identify missing or inaccurate information. The Free AI Check is a quick starting point, not a guarantee of future visibility.

Run the [Free AI Check](https://report.audienceintent.ai/). It asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI the questions your customers ask, shows whether they name you or a competitor, and lists what to fix. It takes about two minutes. No signup is needed to run it.

## AEO vs SEO: Why They're Different and Why You Need Both

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo
Published: 2026-11-05
Summary: Learn how AEO and SEO work together, why Google rankings do not guarantee AI recommendations, and how to split your budget and measure both channels.

SEO helps your business appear in search results; AEO helps it appear in AI answers and recommendations. You need both because ranking first on Google does not guarantee that ChatGPT, Google AI, or Perplexity will recommend you. AEO should work alongside your SEO—not replace the work or the people already helping you rank.

#### AEO vs SEO: What Is the Difference?

Search engine optimization, or SEO, improves your visibility in search results. Answer engine optimization, or AEO, makes your business and content easier for AI systems to find, understand, cite, and recommend.

The simplest distinction is **search rankings versus AI answers**. The work overlaps, but the outcome you measure is different.

| Question | SEO | AEO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is the main goal? | Earn visibility and clicks from search results | Earn accurate mentions, citations, and recommendations in AI answers |
| Where does it show up? | Google and Bing results, including local search | ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, and Perplexity |
| What does the customer do? | Searches, compares results, and may click | Asks a question, reads an answer, and may research further or contact a business |
| What work matters? | Technical health, useful pages, internal links, and credible outside references | The same foundations, plus clear business facts, direct answers, and AI-specific testing |
| What should you measure? | Search impressions, rankings, clicks, leads, and sales | Mentions, citations, recommendations, share of voice, referral traffic, and leads |
| Does success guarantee the other? | No. Strong rankings do not guarantee AI recommendations | No. An AI mention does not guarantee strong search rankings |

These are not completely separate worlds. Google itself combines traditional results with AI answers, and AI systems can use web search to find sources. That is why treating AEO as unrelated to SEO is just as misleading as treating them as identical.

For the wider definition, see [what AEO and GEO are](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/what-is-answer-engine-optimization-aeo-the-complete-guide-for-2026).

#### What SEO Still Does Well

SEO still helps customers find your services, products, locations, and answers through search. The arrival of AI answers changes where attention goes; it does not make your website or search presence unnecessary.

Google handles [more than 5 trillion searches a year](https://searchengineland.com/google-5-trillion-searches-per-year-452928), according to Google in 2025. That is roughly 14 billion searches a day.

People still need to compare providers, check prices, confirm service areas, read product details, and make purchases. Strong service pages, accurate Google Business Profiles, useful articles, and healthy websites support those decisions.

Keep tracking which pages bring qualified visitors and customers. Do not assume that all informational traffic has stopped working, or that commercial and local searches are untouched by AI. Look at your own results by query type and page.

##### Good SEO Gives AEO a Head Start

The technical and content work behind good SEO also helps AI systems discover and interpret your business. You should build on that work rather than pay to repeat it.

The shared foundations include:
- **Accessible pages:** Important content should be available to relevant search and AI crawlers.
- **Clear site structure:** Descriptive headings and internal links help systems find related information.
- **Useful content:** Accurate, specific explanations give both customers and AI systems something worth reading.
- **Credible references:** Relevant links and outside mentions can help establish context and trust.
- **Consistent business facts:** Your name, services, location, and contact information should agree across major profiles.

Schema can help describe your business and pages, but it is not a ranking or recommendation guarantee. Likewise, a third-party domain authority score is not a universal admission requirement for AI visibility.

**If your SEO is solid, you are not starting from zero with AEO.** You are adding a goal, a set of tests, and work aimed at AI answers.

#### Why You Can Rank First on Google and Still Be Invisible in AI

A Google ranking tells you where a page appears for a particular search. It does not tell you whether an AI system will select that page, describe your business accurately, or recommend you for a customer's specific situation.

Consider a roofing company that ranks first for “roof repair Wellington.” A homeowner asks an AI assistant: “Who repairs tile roofs in Wellington and offers emergency help?”

The company's ranking is useful. But its website may never clearly explain that it repairs tile roofs or offers emergency service. Another business may have a page that answers those questions directly, supported by consistent business information elsewhere.

The first business can win the search ranking and still miss the recommendation. That is an example of how the gap can happen—not a rule about which company an AI will choose.

##### What AEO Adds

AEO makes the information needed for a recommendation easier to find and verify. It also checks whether that information is actually showing up in answers.

Useful work includes:
1. **Researching customer questions.** Cover real needs, service areas, costs, limitations, comparisons, and buying decisions—not just short keywords.
2. **Stating business facts clearly.** Explain what you do, whom you serve, and where you operate.
3. **Writing direct answers.** Open a section with the answer, then add details and evidence.
4. **Keeping important facts consistent.** Small name variations do not automatically create separate businesses, but conflicting addresses, phone numbers, or service descriptions can create confusion.
5. **Checking outside information.** AI systems may consult business profiles, publications, reviews, and other sources. Your website is not the only place customers or AI can learn about you.
6. **Testing AI responses over time.** Check whether the right business appears, whether the description is accurate, and which sources are cited.

Do not confuse a citation with a recommendation. An AI can cite an article from your website without recommending your company as a provider.

For practical fixes, read [why ChatGPT skips your business and how to fix it](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/why-chatgpt-doesnt-recommend-your-business-and-how-to-fix-it).

#### Why Add AEO Now?

AI answers are a large enough discovery channel to deserve their own attention. That is a reason to expand your visibility work, not abandon search.

OpenAI reported that ChatGPT had **about 1.2 billion weekly active users in November 2026**, according to [Big Technology](https://www.bigtechnology.com/p/openai-chatgpt-search-is-about-20). Weekly users are not the same as searches or purchase-ready customers, but the scale matters.

AI summaries also change clicking behavior. [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org) found that users clicked a traditional search result in 8% of visits when an AI summary appeared, compared with 15% when one did not.

A separate [Seer Interactive study](https://www.seerinteractive.com/insights/aio-impact-on-google-ctr-september-2025-update) reported organic click-through rates falling from 1.76% to 0.61% for the AI Overview query group it studied—a decline of about 61%.

Those findings describe particular studies, not a guaranteed traffic loss for every business. They do explain why a rankings-only report can miss a change in how customers discover providers.

The response is to measure two things: whether customers can find your pages, and whether AI answers include your business.

#### How Your SEO Provider and AEO Team Should Work Together

Keep your SEO provider if the work is good. Add AI-specific responsibilities to the existing scope or bring in help for the parts the current team does not handle.

Some SEO providers already do substantial AEO work. Others focus on rankings and organic traffic. Ask about deliverables rather than assuming the label tells you everything.

A useful conversation starts with these questions:
- Which customer questions are we testing in AI answers?
- Are we tracking business recommendations as well as website citations?
- Who fixes inaccurate business information?
- Who owns schema, crawler access, and page edits?
- How will we report search results and AI visibility separately?

Use one shared content calendar and one owner for each technical change. If both teams edit a service page independently, you risk duplicate work or conflicting changes.

For example, the SEO team might identify a valuable service query. The AEO team can add related customer questions and check whether AI answers name the business. One improved page can serve both goals.

**AEO is not a threat to your SEO provider. It is another outcome the work should support.**

#### How to Split Your SEO and AEO Budget

Protect the SEO work that brings customers, then fund the gaps in your AI visibility. There is no universal budget split based on business size or a domain authority score.

Start by identifying the actual problem. A blocked website needs technical repairs. A strong website with weak AI visibility needs clearer answers, accurate business facts, and consistent testing. Those are different spending decisions.

##### Illustrative Starting Splits

The percentages below are planning examples for SEO and AEO spending combined—not research benchmarks or percentages of your entire marketing budget. Adjust them to your costs and results.

| Your situation | Example SEO/AEO split | First priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Important pages are missing or difficult to crawl | 75% / 25% | Repair the foundation while establishing an AI baseline |
| SEO brings steady leads, but AI rarely names you | 60% / 40% | Maintain useful SEO work and address AI-specific gaps |
| Search performance is strong and competitors dominate relevant AI answers | 50% / 50% | Test a larger AEO effort without neglecting search |

Shared work should be counted once. A schema repair or an updated service page may support both SEO and AEO; it does not need two separate budgets.

You can use the same approach for staff time. Decide which tasks matter most, assign an owner, and agree on what will be delivered over the next 90 days.

##### Before You Move Money, Check Four Things

Make a budget change only after you understand what you are protecting and what you want to improve.
1. **Current customers:** Which search pages produce qualified inquiries or sales?
2. **Technical problems:** Can relevant crawlers access your important pages?
3. **AI gaps:** Which customer questions name competitors but not you?
4. **Available capacity:** Can your team publish, update, and measure consistently?

You do not need perfect SEO before starting AEO. Fix serious problems first, but basic AI visibility checks and clearer business information can begin immediately.

Review the split after 90 days. Keep spending tied to useful work and observed progress, not a fixed percentage that never changes.

#### How to Measure SEO and AEO Separately

Measure SEO by search discovery and business outcomes. Measure AEO by what appears in AI answers, then connect that visibility to traffic and inquiries where possible.

A single “organic traffic” number cannot explain both.

| Measure | What to track | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEO visibility | Search impressions and rankings for important queries | Whether your pages appear in search |
| SEO visits | Clicks, click-through rate, and organic sessions | Whether search visibility leads to visits |
| SEO outcomes | Qualified inquiries, sales, and conversion rate | Whether those visits help the business |
| AI mentions | Answers that name your business | Whether AI includes you |
| AI citations | Answers that link to your website or another source about you | Which sources support the answer |
| AI recommendations | Answers that suggest your business for the customer's need | Whether you are being presented as a provider to consider |
| AI share of voice | Your share of tracked business mentions compared with competitors | How much of the measured conversation you receive |
| AI outcomes | Identifiable referral visits, inquiries, and sales | What can be connected to AI discovery |

##### Make the AI Test Repeatable

Use a stable set of customer questions and record the platform, date, location assumptions, and results. AI answers can change, so one favorable screenshot is not a trend.

Track discovery questions, comparisons, service-area questions, and specific customer needs. Do not test only prompts that already contain your business name.

Define each metric before reporting it. For example, share of voice can mean your business's mentions divided by all tracked business mentions. That is different from the percentage of answers containing your name. Keep the same definition and competitor set over time.

##### Be Honest About Attribution

AI discovery does not always produce a trackable click. Someone may read a recommendation, search your name later, and call.

GA4 can identify some visits from known AI referrers, but it will not reveal every AI-assisted customer journey. Google AI visits may also appear within Google organic reporting rather than as a separate AI source.

Report identifiable AI referrals, search performance, and customer-reported discovery separately. Do not add overlapping totals together or assume every branded search came from AI.

For a fuller measurement plan, see [how to measure AEO campaign success](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-measure-the-success-of-an-aeo-campaign-metrics-kpis-and-benchmarks-for-2026).

#### What to Do in the First 90 Days

Use the first 90 days to establish a baseline, fix important gaps, and repeat the tests. Do not treat it as a deadline for a guaranteed recommendation.

##### First Month: Establish the Facts

Check your current search performance and AI visibility. Confirm crawler access, important business details, service pages, Google Business Profile information, and the customer questions your content should answer.

##### Second Month: Publish and Improve

Add useful answers where information is missing. Update older pages, correct conflicting facts, and coordinate changes with your SEO provider. Check which pages AI systems cite and whether the business descriptions are accurate.

##### Third Month: Review the Pattern

Compare repeated tests against the baseline. Look for relevant mentions, accurate recommendations, citations, competitor changes, and identifiable inquiries—not just a larger count of low-value mentions.

**Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis.** Results vary, and nobody can guarantee an appearance in a specific AI answer.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

##### Is AEO just SEO with a new name?

No. SEO focuses on visibility in search results, while AEO focuses on visibility in AI answers and recommendations. They share technical and content foundations, but AEO adds AI-specific question research, response testing, and measurement. Good work can support both without making them identical.

##### Do I need to replace my SEO provider to do AEO?

No. Keep a provider that does good work. Ask which AI-specific tasks and measurements are already included, then assign any gaps. Coordinate page edits, technical changes, and content plans so the teams do not duplicate work.

##### Can I rank first on Google and still be invisible in AI?

Yes. Ranking first for a search does not guarantee that an AI system will select your page or recommend your business for a related question. AI visibility depends on the question, available sources, business information, and the answer generated at that time.

##### How much should I spend on AEO versus SEO?

There is no universal split. Protect SEO work that brings qualified customers, fix serious website problems, and fund the AI visibility gaps you can identify. Set a 90-day plan, count shared work once, and adjust spending based on results rather than a domain authority threshold.

##### How long does AEO take to work?

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why AudienceIntent starts with 90 days. No provider can guarantee inclusion in a specific answer.

##### How do I measure AEO if people do not click?

Track business mentions, citations, recommendations, and share of voice across a consistent set of customer questions. Add identifiable AI referral traffic, inquiries, and customer-reported discovery. Report these separately because an AI mention is not a website visit, and not every AI-assisted sale is traceable.

##### Do local businesses need both SEO and AEO?

Yes. Local SEO helps customers find your business through search and maps. AEO helps make your services, location, and suitability clear in AI answers. Accurate business facts, useful service pages, and a well-maintained Google Business Profile support both, without guaranteeing a recommendation.

#### What Is AI Recommended™?

AI Recommended™ is a monthly answer engine optimization service, often called AEO. Its purpose is to make your business easier for AI systems to find, understand, and recommend when customers ask relevant questions.

AudienceIntent offers one service: AI Recommended™. It is work done for you by a real team, not self-serve software or a dashboard you have to manage yourself.

That describes the goal, not a guaranteed placement. AudienceIntent promises the work, done properly every month, and an honest report. No provider can control which business an AI system names in a particular answer.

#### How Does AI Decide Which Businesses to Recommend?

AI systems can use information from your website and outside sources to answer recommendation questions. Clear business details, useful answers, and consistent information help them understand whether your business fits what someone needs.

For example, someone asking “Which food tour should I book in this city?” may care about location, tour length, dietary options, price, and availability. A page that answers those questions gives an AI system more useful information than a page that only says “unforgettable experiences.”

Useful information includes:
- **What you offer:** Specific services, products, prices where available, and who you serve.
- **Where you operate:** Accurate locations, service areas, hours, and contact details.
- **Answers to customer questions:** Clear explanations of choices, costs, limits, and next steps.
- **Supporting information:** Relevant business profiles, independent coverage, reviews, and other sources that may help confirm facts.

There is no published universal formula or fixed number of sources that guarantees a recommendation. Different systems can use different sources, and answers can change with the question, location, or timing.

For more detail, read [how AI decides which businesses to recommend](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-ai-search-engines-like-chatgpt-decide-which-businesses-to-recommend-and-how-to-be-one-of-them).

#### What Does AI Recommended™ Include Every Month?

AI Recommended™ includes eight recurring parts, plus brand fixes. The work covers website access, technical improvements, useful content, daily tracking, and regular communication.

##### 1. Open to Crawlers

AudienceIntent checks the settings and files that help crawlers access and discover your website, including robots.txt, llms.txt, and sitemaps. Useful content cannot help much if relevant systems cannot reach it.

The aim is to remove avoidable access problems and make important pages discoverable. These files do not force an AI system to index a page, cite it, or recommend your business. An llms.txt file is not a universal requirement for AI visibility.

##### 2. Website Fixes: Schema, Sitemap, and On-Page Improvements

AudienceIntent makes website fixes that help explain your business and its pages more clearly. This includes schema, sitemap work, and on-page improvements.

Schema provides structured information about a business or page. On-page work can make headings, service descriptions, locations, and answers easier to understand. The goal is accurate, readable information—not adding markup that promises a ranking or citation.

##### 3. Customer Question Research

AudienceIntent researches the questions customers ask when choosing a business like yours. Those questions guide content topics and updates.

A customer may ask which provider serves their area, what a service costs, how two options differ, or what to check before booking. Research helps focus the work on real buying questions rather than publishing articles simply to fill a schedule.

##### 4. Four New Articles a Month

AudienceIntent creates four new articles each month to answer relevant customer questions. Clear explanations give both readers and AI systems useful material to work with.

Depending on the business, topics may cover service choices, costs, comparisons, common concerns, or location-specific needs. Each article should make its answer easy to find and support factual claims. Publishing four articles does not mean four guaranteed AI citations.

##### 5. Four Older Pages Updated a Month

AudienceIntent updates four older pages each month. This keeps existing information useful instead of focusing only on new content.

Older pages may contain outdated details, incomplete answers, unclear service descriptions, or missed customer questions. Updating them helps the website present a more accurate picture of the business. The monthly commitment is four page updates, alongside the four new articles.

##### 6. Weekly Visibility Report With 50 Prompts Tracked Daily

AudienceIntent tracks 50 customer-style prompts daily and provides a weekly visibility report. The paid service tracks ChatGPT, Google AI—including AI Overviews and AI Mode—and Perplexity.

Daily tracking gives a broader view than checking one question once. The weekly report helps you review changes over time without treating a single answer as a permanent result. AI answers can vary, so repeated observation matters.

##### 7. Competitor Tracking for Up to Five Competitors

AudienceIntent tracks up to five competitors so you can compare your visibility with other businesses customers may be considering. This helps show whether an answer names your business, a competitor, or neither.

A competitor’s appearance is useful context, not proof that copying its content will produce the same result. The comparison helps identify questions and topics where your business needs clearer or more complete information.

##### 8. Monthly Progress Call and Shared Slack Channel

AI Recommended™ includes a monthly progress call and a shared Slack channel. You have a way to discuss the work, ask questions, and review progress with the team.

The call connects the reporting with the work being done. Slack provides a shared place for communication between calls. You do not have to interpret a software dashboard and decide what to do on your own.

##### Brand Fixes Are Included Too

AudienceIntent also optimizes your Google Business Profile and works on consistent business name, address, and phone information across major profiles. These details help people and AI systems identify the same business correctly.

This is specific business-information work. It is not digital PR, third-party content placement, review management, review-request automation, or an ongoing directory-management service.

#### How Should You Read the Visibility Report?

Look for patterns across repeated checks, not a single favorable answer. A useful review asks whether your business appears more consistently for relevant questions and how that compares with competitors.

It also helps to keep three terms separate:
- **Mention:** An AI answer names your business.
- **Citation:** An AI answer references a source, often through a link.
- **AI traffic:** Someone visits your website from an AI platform.

These measures describe different things. More mentions do not automatically mean more visits, and more visits do not automatically mean more sales. A citation can reference your page without recommending your business.

## How Much Does AI Search Visibility Cost?

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-much-does-ai-search-visibility-cost
Published: 2026-09-01
Summary: AI Recommended is $1,997/month, flat, no matter your size. See what's actually included and why most agencies won't give you a straight number.

When a customer asks ChatGPT or Perplexity to recommend a plumber, a financial advisor, or a metal fabricator, one business gets named. The rest get nothing. That reality is driving a wave of business owners to ask a very practical question: what does it actually cost to show up in those answers?

The short answer is: it depends on who you hire, what they actually do, and whether they lock you into a contract before you see a single result.

**The honest range:** AI search visibility services run anywhere from $1,000 to $25,000+ per month in 2026, depending on scope, competition, and provider. Most local businesses don't need the high end. But most also don't know what they're buying at the low end.

This guide breaks down what the market charges, what you actually get at each price point, and what to look for before you sign anything.

> **TL;DR**
> 
> -   AI search visibility (AEO/GEO) services run $1,000-$25,000+/month in 2026
>     
> -   Most local businesses fit the $1,997-$5,000/month range for meaningful results
>     
> -   AI Recommended™ from AudienceIntent is $1,997/month for a 90-day minimum, then $997/month month to month — or $5,000 upfront for the first 90 days (saves $991)
>     
> -   Most agencies require 6-12 month contracts with setup fees of $2,500-$12,000+
>     
> -   AI traffic converts at 4.4x the rate of standard organic traffic — the ROI case is real
>     
> -   Only 12% of pages cited by ChatGPT rank in Google's top 10, so SEO alone won't get you there
>     

#### Why AI Search Visibility Is a Separate Investment From SEO

Most business owners assume their existing SEO investment covers AI search. It doesn't — and the data makes that gap hard to ignore.

[Research shows that only 12% of pages cited by ChatGPT rank in Google's top 10](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo)). These are almost entirely separate ecosystems. A business can rank on page one of Google and still be completely invisible when a customer asks an AI assistant for a recommendation.

**Why the gap exists:** Google ranks pages based on links, keywords, and technical signals. AI assistants cite sources based on authority, structured content, third-party mentions, and how well a business answers the specific questions people are actually asking. The optimization playbook is different.

The scale of the shift matters too. [Since AI Overviews appeared in Google search results, organic click-through rates have dropped 61%](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/ai-recommended-your-competitor-not-you-heres-the-revenue-math). Traffic that used to flow to websites is now being absorbed by AI-generated answers. Businesses that aren't in those answers aren't just missing a new channel — they're losing ground they already had.

##### What AI Search Visibility Services Actually Do

When you pay for AI search visibility, you're paying for a specific set of activities that most traditional SEO agencies don't do:
- **Crawlability and structure:** Making sure AI systems can read, understand, and trust your business information
- **Content that answers real questions:** Creating pages and copy that directly answer what customers ask AI assistants
- **Third-party citation building:** Getting your business mentioned and cited on the external sources AI engines pull from — directories, review platforms, editorial sites
- **Prompt tracking and reporting:** Monitoring which AI prompts your business appears in and which ones you're missing
- **Ongoing optimization:** Adjusting based on what's working, what's not, and how AI engines are evolving

[85% of brand mentions in AI answers come from third-party sources](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines) — not from the business's own website. That's the core of why this work is different from SEO, and why it requires a different kind of investment.

#### What AI Search Visibility Actually Costs in 2026

The market for AI search visibility services is still maturing, which means pricing is all over the place. Here's an honest look at what different tiers actually deliver.

| Service Tier | Typical Monthly Cost | Contract Terms | What You're Getting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DIY tools / basic audits | $99 – $500/mo | Month-to-month | Software access, no execution |
| Freelance / project work | $150 – $2,000 (one-time) | Per project | Single-page optimization, basic schema |
| Entry-level retainers | $1,000 – $2,500/mo | Often 6-12 months | Foundational monitoring, limited content |
| Mid-market retainers | $2,000 – $8,000/mo | 6-12 month contracts | Active optimization, content, citation work |
| Enterprise programs | $10,000 – $30,000+/mo | Annual contracts | Full-scale campaigns, PR, deep reporting |

*Source:* [*The Digital Elevator AEO/GEO Pricing Guide, 2026*](https://thedigitalelevator.com/blog/aeo-and-geo-pricing-guide/)*;* [*Stackmatix AEO Agency Pricing Report, 2026*](https://www.stackmatix.com/blog/aeo-agency-pricing-costs)

##### What the Low End Actually Buys You

The $99-$500/month category is largely software — tools that track your AI visibility without doing anything to improve it. Some SEO platforms have added AI monitoring dashboards and rebranded them as AEO services. That's not the same thing.

Entry-level retainers in the $1,000-$2,500 range typically cover a one-time audit and some foundational fixes. The issue is that AI visibility is not a one-time problem. Prompts change, AI engines update their sourcing behavior, and competitors keep building citations. A one-time fix doesn't hold.

##### What the Mid-Market Range Gets Right

The $2,000-$8,000/month tier is where serious execution happens. This is where agencies are actively creating content, building third-party citations, monitoring prompt performance, and adjusting strategy month over month.

**The catch:** most mid-market agencies require 6-12 month contracts. Setup fees at this tier typically run $2,500 to $12,000 before the monthly retainer even starts. For a local business, that's a significant commitment before you've seen a single result.

##### The Part Most Agencies Don't Advertise

Most agencies at every tier are built around enterprise or B2B SaaS clients. Their pricing, minimums, and timelines reflect that. A local HVAC company, a franchise owner, or a professional services firm has different needs — and most agencies aren't set up to serve them efficiently at a price that makes sense.

#### How AI Recommended™ Is Priced — and How It Compares

## No One Can Guarantee You'll Be the Number 1 Answer in AI Search. Here's What Actually Works.

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/no-one-can-guarantee-youll-be-the-number-1-answer-in-ai-search-heres-what-actually-works
Published: 2026-07-08
Summary: No one can guarantee number 1 AI search placement. Learn what actually improves AI visibility and run the Free AI Check.

Something real is happening in how customers find businesses. More people are skipping the search results page entirely and asking AI directly: "Who's the best HVAC company near me?" "What's the top-rated accountant in Austin?" "Which marketing agency should I hire?" ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI are now answering those questions — and recommending specific businesses by name.

That shift is significant. And it has created a predictable side effect: a wave of vendors promising to put your business at the top of those answers.

"We'll make you number 1 in ChatGPT." "Guaranteed AI recommendations in 7 days." "We control what AI says about your brand."

**These promises are not real.** Not because the vendors are necessarily dishonest, but because the underlying claim is technically impossible. AI search does not work like a search results page. There is no "position 1" to sell you. There is no lever to pull that forces ChatGPT to recommend your business above everyone else.

This article explains why, what actually does influence AI visibility, and how to tell the difference between a vendor doing real work and one selling certainty that does not exist.

#### Why AI Search Cannot Be Guaranteed

AI search visibility is not a fixed position you can purchase or permanently hold. Every answer an AI system generates is produced fresh, in real time, based on a combination of signals that shift constantly.

The same question asked by two different people can produce two different answers. The same business can appear in one AI platform's response and be absent from another's. A recommendation you see today may not be there tomorrow.

Here is what actually determines what AI systems say:
- **The exact wording of the question.** "Best plumber near me" and "most affordable plumber in \[city\]" can produce entirely different results.
- **The user's location.** AI systems with location awareness surface different businesses depending on where the query originates.
- **Search history and personalization.** Some AI systems factor in prior interactions and user context.
- **Whether the platform uses live web results.** Perplexity pulls from the live web. Some ChatGPT responses do not. The underlying data source changes the answer.
- **Model updates.** AI companies update their models regularly. A business that appeared in answers last month may not appear after a model refresh.
- **Source availability and freshness.** If the sources an AI system draws from are outdated or missing, your business may not appear even if you deserve to.
- **Third-party mentions.** What other sites, directories, and publications say about your business matters — often more than your own website.
- **Reviews and reputation signals.** Volume, recency, and sentiment of reviews influence how confidently AI systems describe a business.
- **Content clarity.** If your website is vague about what you do, who you serve, and where you operate, AI systems will be vague about you too.
- **Entity consistency.** Inconsistent business name, address, or category information across the web creates confusion that reduces AI confidence.
- **Trust signals across the web.** Authority, citations, backlinks, and third-party validation all contribute to whether an AI system feels confident recommending you.

> **The core problem with "guaranteed AI rankings":** There is no fixed index to rank in. AI answers are generated, not retrieved. No vendor has write access to ChatGPT's outputs, Perplexity's citations, or Google's AI Overviews. Anyone claiming otherwise is selling something they cannot deliver.

AI search is dynamic, contextual, and constantly changing. That does not mean you cannot influence it. It means you cannot control it — and any vendor who tells you otherwise is not being straight with you.

#### The Promises Buyers Should Avoid

As AI search has grown, so has the number of vendors claiming to dominate it. Some of these claims are aggressive marketing. Others are outright misleading. Here are the red flags to watch for — and why each one should give you pause.

| Red-Flag Claim | Why It's Misleading |
| --- | --- |
| "We'll make you number 1 in ChatGPT." | There is no number 1 position in ChatGPT. Answers are generated per query, not ranked in a fixed index. |
| "You'll appear in AI answers in 7 days." | Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. |
| "We can control what AI says about your brand." | No vendor has access to the output layer of any AI system. You can influence what AI says by improving your signals; you cannot dictate it. |
| "AI visibility is just SEO with a new name." | Only [12% of pages cited by ChatGPT rank in Google's top 10](https://audienceintent.ai/insights). These are different ecosystems with different signals and different citation logic. |
| "You only need one article to rank in AI." | AI systems draw from dozens of signals: reviews, directories, third-party mentions, structured data, and more. One piece of content is not a strategy. |
| "We guarantee AI recommendations." | Guarantees require control. No vendor controls AI outputs. Any guarantee here is either a misrepresentation or a meaningless promise with no accountability behind it. |
| "We can erase competitors from AI answers." | This is not how AI systems work. You cannot remove a competitor from an AI's training data or live search results. The only legitimate play is to become more credible than they are. |

The pattern across all of these claims is the same: they sell certainty in a system that does not offer it. The businesses that get hurt are the ones that pay for a guarantee, see no results, and then distrust the entire category of AI visibility work — including the legitimate kind.

**What to ask instead:** "What signals do you improve, how do you measure them, and what does progress look like over 90 days?" A vendor with a real process can answer that clearly.

#### What Actually Influences AI Visibility

If you cannot control AI search, you can still shape it. The signals below are what AI systems actually use to decide whether to mention, cite, or recommend a business. Improving them does not guarantee placement — but neglecting them almost guarantees you will be invisible.

##### Signals That Build AI Visibility Over Time

**Clear positioning.** AI systems describe businesses in the language they find on the web. If your website is vague about what you do, where you serve, and who you help, AI will be equally vague — or skip you entirely.

**Consistent brand entity information.** Your business name, address, phone number, and category should match exactly across your website, Google Business Profile, directories, and third-party listings. Inconsistency creates doubt. AI systems prefer confidence.

**Helpful, citation-worthy content.** AI systems cite pages that directly answer the questions people are asking. Service pages, location pages, FAQ content, comparison guides, and proof-based case studies all give AI something concrete to reference.

**Review volume and sentiment.** [Research consistently shows](https://audienceintent.ai/insights) that AI systems factor in reviews when forming recommendations. A business with 200 recent, detailed reviews is more citable than one with 12 old ones. Sentiment matters too — not just star ratings, but the language customers use.

**Third-party mentions.** Approximately 85% of brand mentions in AI answers come from third-party sources, not the brand's own website. Industry directories, local publications, partner sites, and review platforms all contribute to the picture AI systems build of your business.

**Directory and profile consistency.** Yelp, BBB, Angi, Houzz, industry-specific directories — these are sources AI systems pull from. Being present and accurate across them matters.

**Structured data.** Schema markup on your website helps AI systems understand exactly what your business is, what it offers, and where it operates. It reduces ambiguity.

**FAQ coverage.** AI systems are built to answer questions. Pages that directly answer the questions your customers ask are more likely to be cited than pages that only describe what you sell.

**Proof points and case studies.** Specific, verifiable results build credibility. "Craft Food Tours saw traffic from AI increase by 312% in 90 days" is more citable than "we deliver results."

**Freshness and ongoing updates.** Stale content signals a stale business. AI systems that use live web results favor recently updated pages and active profiles.

**Authority from trusted sources.** Links and mentions from authoritative, relevant sources increase how much weight AI systems give your content.

The goal here is not to trick AI systems into recommending you. The goal is to become easier to understand, easier to verify, and easier to cite. A business that is clear, consistent, and well-documented across the web is a business AI can recommend with confidence.

#### What Honest AI Visibility Work Looks Like

A credible AI visibility engagement does not start with promises. It starts with a baseline — an honest assessment of where you actually stand before anyone claims they can improve anything.

Here is what a legitimate process includes:
1. **Auditing current AI descriptions.** Running structured prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI to see how each platform currently describes your business, what it gets right, what it gets wrong, and where you are absent entirely.
2. **Tracking visibility across platforms.** Not just one AI, not just one prompt. A real measurement framework covers multiple platforms, multiple question types, and multiple competitor comparisons.
3. **Identifying competitor gaps.** Where are competitors appearing that you are not? What are they doing that you are not? Competitive gaps are often the fastest path to improvement.
4. **Finding missing proof and unclear positioning.** Where is your content vague? What questions are customers asking that your website does not answer? What proof points are missing that would make AI more confident citing you?
5. **Improving citable pages.** Rewriting or building service pages, location pages, FAQ content, and case studies that give AI systems something concrete and credible to reference.
6. **Strengthening reviews and reputation signals.** Building a consistent review strategy that increases volume, recency, and the quality of language customers use to describe your business.
7. **Building third-party validation.** Earning mentions, citations, and listings across the sources AI systems draw from.
8. **Measuring over time.** Tracking visibility, share of voice, citations, sentiment, and answer quality across platforms — and reporting on what is improving, what is not, and why.

> **The key distinction:** Visibility should be measured over a period of weeks and months, not judged from a single prompt on a single day. One AI answer on one afternoon tells you almost nothing. A trend line over 90 days tells you whether the work is compounding.

This is not a shortcut. It is a compounding strategy. The businesses that build AI visibility the right way are the ones that become harder to displace over time — because their signals are genuinely stronger, not because someone gamed a system that cannot be gamed.

#### The Real Goal Is Trust, Not Instant Rankings

Here is the thing that gets lost in all the talk about AI rankings and number 1 placements: AI systems are not trying to rank businesses. They are trying to answer questions confidently.

When someone asks ChatGPT for a recommendation, the system is not consulting a leaderboard. It is synthesizing everything it knows about the available options and choosing the one it can describe with the most confidence. The business that wins is not the one with the loudest marketing. It is the one with the clearest, most consistent, most well-documented presence across the web.

That is a fundamentally different game than traditional SEO. And it rewards a fundamentally different kind of work.

The brands that will win in AI search over the next few years are not the ones that find a loophole. They are the ones that become genuinely easier to trust: easier for AI systems to understand, easier for AI systems to verify, and easier for AI systems to recommend without hedging.

**The goal is not to force AI to recommend you. The goal is to become the kind of business AI can confidently recommend.**

That means doing the unglamorous work: cleaning up your entity data, building out your FAQ content, earning more reviews, getting mentioned in more places, and keeping your information fresh and accurate. None of it is a hack. All of it compounds.

Customers who find you through AI search are already in a high-trust state. They asked for a recommendation and your name came up. That traffic converts at [4.4 times the rate of standard organic search](https://audienceintent.ai/insights) — 14.2% versus 2.8%. The prize is real. The path to it is just not the one being sold in most cold emails right now.

#### How to Evaluate an AI Visibility Company

Before you hire anyone to work on your AI search visibility, run them through this checklist. A vendor doing real work should be able to answer every one of these questions clearly.

##### The Buyer's Checklist
- **Do they explain what they can and cannot control?** Any vendor who claims to control AI outputs is either confused or misleading you. Honest vendors are specific about influence versus control.
- **Do they measure visibility across multiple AI platforms?** ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI behave differently. A vendor measuring only one is giving you an incomplete picture.
- **Do they track competitors?** Your AI visibility is relative, not absolute. If your competitors are appearing where you are not, that gap matters. A credible vendor tracks both.
- **Do they show citations and sources?** Can they show you which pages are being cited, by which platforms, in response to which questions? If the answer is vague, the measurement is vague.
- **Do they separate visibility from rankings?** AI visibility is about citations, mentions, sentiment, and share of voice — not "positions." A vendor conflating the two does not understand the space.
- **Do they talk about reviews, proof, and third-party validation?** If a vendor's entire pitch is about content and ignores reputation signals, they are missing more than half the picture.
- **Do they avoid guaranteed placement claims?** This is the simplest filter. If they guarantee number 1 placement in any AI system, stop the conversation.
- **Do they provide a baseline before making promises?** No credible vendor should promise improvement without first measuring where you stand. A baseline is not optional — it is the foundation of everything that follows.

The right vendor will welcome these questions. They will have clear answers, documented processes, and a reporting framework that shows you exactly what is being measured and how it is changing over time.

A steady approach to earning honest reviews can help a business's AI visibility.
