## How to Get Your Business Recommended by AI Search Engines

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines
Published: 2026-11-01
Summary: Learn how to get your business recommended by ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity with practical steps, business-specific tips, and honest tracking advice.

To get your business recommended by AI search engines, make your business details accurate, keep your website accessible, and publish clear answers to customer questions. Support those facts with credible independent sources, then test the same questions across ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity. These steps can improve your chances, but nobody can guarantee a place in a specific AI answer.

This work is called Answer Engine Optimization, or AEO. It builds on good website and search practices rather than replacing them. For the differences, see [AEO vs. SEO](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo).

#### Step 1: Find Out Whether AI Already Recommends You

Start with a fixed list of questions your customers ask before buying. Record which businesses each platform recommends, whether the details are correct, and which pages it cites.

Choose 10–20 questions from customer emails, sales conversations, support requests, and common objections. Include different buying needs, not just variations of “best business near me.”

| Customer need | Example prompt |
| --- | --- |
| Find a local provider | “Who repairs air conditioners in [city]?” |
| Check a requirement | “Which dentists in [city] accept new patients on Saturdays?” |
| Compare products | “Which protein powders under $40 are dairy-free?” |
| Understand cost | “What does a roof replacement in [city] usually cost?” |
| Compare alternatives | “How does [product] compare with [alternative] for [specific use]?” |

Run the relevant questions in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI. For Google, distinguish AI Overviews from AI Mode, and record when no AI Overview appears. Specify your city instead of relying only on “near me.”

Save the date, exact prompt, platform, location, answer, and cited URLs. Keep three outcomes separate:
- **Mention:** Your business is named.
- **Recommendation:** Your business is presented as an option for the customer's need.
- **Citation:** A source is linked. That source might be your website or a third-party page about you.

One answer is a snapshot, not a final verdict. Results can change with wording, location, account context, and time.

For a faster starting point, the [Free AI Check](https://report.audienceintent.ai/) asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI the questions your customers ask. It shows whether they name you or a competitor and lists what to fix. It takes about two minutes, with no signup needed to run it.

#### Step 2: Fix Inaccurate Business Details

Make your business easy to identify across your website and major profiles. Prioritize wrong phone numbers, old addresses, outdated hours, and unclear services before minor formatting differences.

Create one reference sheet with your business name, address where appropriate, phone number, website, hours, services, and service areas. Compare it with your website's contact page, footer, and About page, then your major profiles.

For local businesses, start at [Google Business Profile](https://business.google.com). Check:
- Your real business name, without added keywords.
- The most specific accurate primary category and relevant secondary categories.
- Current opening hours and holiday hours.
- Cities or areas you actually serve.
- Service descriptions, appointment requirements, and prices where applicable.
- Accurate photos of your location, team, or work.

Service-area businesses should follow Google's address-display rules rather than publishing a private home address just for consistency.

Next, check relevant profiles such as Yelp, Apple Maps, Bing Places, Facebook, and industry directories. A dental practice might check Healthgrades; a law firm might check Avvo. You do not need a listing on every directory.

For an online business, focus on a consistent brand name, contact information, product descriptions, and policies. Do not invent a local presence.

Accurate details help customers and search systems identify the right business. They are not a documented guarantee that AI will choose you over a competitor.

#### Step 3: Make Your Website Accessible to Search Crawlers

Your important pages must be accessible before search-based AI systems can use them reliably. Check crawling, indexing, and page rendering before spending heavily on new content.

Ask whoever maintains your website to review these basics:
- **robots.txt:** Confirm that intended search crawlers are not blocked from public pages.
- **Indexing controls:** Remove accidental `noindex` instructions from pages meant to appear in search.
- **XML sitemap:** Include current, canonical URLs and submit it through the relevant search webmaster tools.
- **Page access:** Fix broken pages, login walls, and security rules that block legitimate crawlers.
- **Visible text:** Make essential service and product details available as readable page content, not only inside images or inaccessible widgets.
- **Internal links:** Link to important pages from navigation or relevant content so they can be discovered.

Search crawling and model-training permissions are not the same thing. Review each crawler's purpose rather than allowing every bot without checking.

For Google AI features, [Google's Search Central guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) says a page must be indexed and eligible to appear in Search with a snippet. Meeting those conditions does not guarantee inclusion.

An `llms.txt` file can be an optional experiment, but evidence that it increases recommendations is limited. It does not replace robots.txt, sitemaps, indexable pages, or useful content, and Google does not require it for AI-feature eligibility.

#### Step 4: Add Accurate Structured Data

Use structured data to describe what is already visible on your pages. Schema can help systems interpret your business, products, and articles, but it is not a shortcut to AI recommendations.

Choose types that fit the page:

| Page or business type | Useful schema to consider |
| --- | --- |
| Local business | LocalBusiness or a more specific subtype |
| Non-local company | Organization |
| Individual service | Service |
| Product page | Product and applicable offer details |
| Article or guide | Article or BlogPosting |

The [LocalBusiness schema reference](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness) describes fields such as name, address, telephone, and opening hours. Keep those values aligned with the page and your actual business details.

For products, keep prices and availability current. Do not add invented ratings, credentials, or claims to markup.

A useful FAQ section does not need FAQPage markup to be readable. Google's FAQ rich-result eligibility is restricted, so adding that markup does not mean a business will receive a special search display.

Check Google-supported markup with [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results). Passing a test does not guarantee a rich result, citation, or recommendation.

#### Step 5: Rewrite Important Pages to Answer Real Questions

Make each important page answer a specific customer question immediately. Follow the answer with the details someone needs to decide whether your business is a good fit.

Start with your main service or product pages before publishing a large batch of articles. Each page should explain:
1. What the service or product does.
2. Who it is suitable for, including important limitations.
3. Where it is available.
4. What it costs, or what changes the price.
5. How long delivery, treatment, or completion usually takes.
6. What evidence supports your claims.

A service-page opening might follow this template:

> “[Business] provides [specific service] in [service area]. The service includes [scope], with pricing based on [main factors].”

Replace every placeholder with a fact you can support. “Licensed contractor serving [county]” is more useful than “the area's leading experts,” provided the license and service area are accurate.

Then answer the questions customers ask most often: “How much does it cost?”, “How long does it take?”, “Which option suits me?”, and “What happens next?” Use descriptive headings, short paragraphs, and tables where they make comparisons easier.

Include relevant authorship, qualifications, original examples, and sources. For health, legal, or financial topics, have a qualified person review the material.

Publish new articles when they answer a question your existing pages do not cover. Avoid near-identical city pages or thin articles written only to repeat a phrase. There is no required word count or FAQ count that earns an AI citation.

#### Step 6: Support Your Claims With Independent Evidence

Give customers and AI systems ways to verify what you say about your business. Relevant reviews, professional credentials, association profiles, and independent coverage can provide that supporting evidence.

Start by inspecting the sources cited in your baseline answers. If several recommendations refer to an industry association, review platform, or buying guide, check whether that source contains accurate information about your business.

Practical tasks for your own team include:
- Correcting outdated facts on profiles you control.
- Keeping professional licenses and association memberships verifiable.
- Publishing case studies with named results and permission.
- Sharing genuine expertise with relevant publications when an opportunity arises.
- Asking for honest customer reviews where the platform permits solicitation.

Do not buy reviews, require positive ratings, or coach customers to make claims they cannot support. Review policies differ by platform; some discourage direct review requests.

Detailed feedback can explain the service a customer received and the circumstances in which it helped. But there is no proven review threshold that guarantees an AI recommendation, and no universal rule that reviews matter more than backlinks.

Review collection and media outreach are separate tasks from AudienceIntent's service. More mentions are not automatically better; relevant, accurate evidence matters more than being listed everywhere.

#### Step 7: Measure Recommendations and Customer Actions Separately

Track AI answers directly, then use analytics to see whether identifiable visits turn into inquiries or purchases. A growing mention count does not automatically mean growing sales.

Rerun your fixed prompt set on a consistent schedule. Compare trends across several checks rather than treating one changed answer as proof of success or failure.

| Measure | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| Mentions | How often your business is named in the tested answers |
| Recommendations | How often your business is suggested for the customer's need |
| Citations | Links to your pages or sources that support facts about you |
| Competitor presence | Which competitors appear for the same questions |
| Accuracy | Whether the answers describe your business correctly |
| Customer actions | Identifiable visits, inquiries, bookings, and purchases |

In Google Analytics 4, inspect session sources such as `chatgpt.com` and `perplexity.ai`, landing pages, and key events. These reports will not capture every AI-influenced customer. Referrer information can be missing, and Google AI traffic may appear within Google organic rather than as a separate channel.

Also ask new customers how they found you. Someone may see an AI recommendation and later search your name or call directly.

For a fuller framework, see [how to measure AEO success](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-measure-the-success-of-an-aeo-campaign-metrics-kpis-and-benchmarks-for-2026).

##### Does AI referral traffic convert better?

Published conversion studies vary, so use your own results rather than a universal AI conversion promise. Industry, attribution, and the definition of a conversion all change the comparison.

[First Page Sage's analysis](https://firstpagesage.com/seo-blog/conversion-rate-benchmarks/) of 218 sites reports visitor-to-lead rates of 4.7% for ChatGPT, 4.1% for Perplexity, and 1.9% for Google organic. By contrast, [Usermaven's B2B SaaS study](https://usermaven.com/research/ai-search-attribution-b2b-saas) of 150 websites found identifiable AI referrals represented 0.88% of sessions, with a same-session conversion rate of about 1.76%.

These are different samples and measures, not interchangeable benchmarks. Track the customer actions that matter to your business.

#### Step 8: Keep the Work Going for at Least 90 Days

Keep checking accuracy, improving useful pages, and measuring the same questions. Initial discovery and steady recommendations happen on different timelines.

Use the first week to establish your baseline, correct major business-data errors, check crawler access, and improve a priority page. That is a work schedule, not a promise of results in seven days.

| Platform | Realistic timing |
| --- | --- |
| Perplexity | Can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks |
| ChatGPT | Usually takes two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis |
| Google AI | Usually takes two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis |

These are expectations, not guarantees. [Google notes](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) that recrawling can take days to months. A crawl, an indexed page, a citation, and a business recommendation are different events.

Each month, review questions you are still missing, update outdated pages, and publish answers where genuine gaps remain. Change prices, hours, stock information, and service areas when they change—not just on a reporting schedule.

For context, Vault Metal's AI mentions went from 169 to 7,808 (+4,520%), and citations went from 3 to 751 in 90 days. [Read the Vault Metal case study](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-vault-metal-went-from-invisible-in-ai-to-7-808-mentions-in-90-days). Craft Food Tours saw traffic from AI increase by 312% in 90 days. These are individual client results, not forecasts for another business.

#### Platform-by-Platform Notes

Use the same accurate business facts across platforms, but check each platform's answers and sources separately. There is no published formula that reliably predicts which business every assistant will recommend.

##### ChatGPT

Focus on accessible, specific information that can support a recommendation when ChatGPT searches the web. Check whether its answers use your website, independent sources, or both.

A source citation does not necessarily mean ChatGPT recommends that source's business. Also, not every answer uses live search. Do not assume a website update must wait for a model-training cycle before it can appear in a search-based answer.

##### Google AI: AI Overviews and AI Mode

Maintain Google Search eligibility and accurate business information. Google's [AI-feature guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) says there are no additional technical requirements beyond its established Search requirements.

For local businesses, keep Google Business Profile current. For retailers, maintain accurate product pages and applicable product feeds. Neither a complete profile nor valid schema guarantees selection.

##### Perplexity

Use Perplexity's source links to see which pages support its answers. Look for missing facts, outdated information, and relevant sources that describe competitors more clearly.

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. That does not mean every newly discovered page will be cited or that its business will be recommended.

##### A brief note on Claude and Gemini

Claude and the standalone Gemini assistant can also answer business questions, and available search features affect the sources they can use. Gemini is not interchangeable with Google's AI Overviews or AI Mode.

These are educational notes, not additional platforms tracked by AudienceIntent's paid service.

#### Adjust the Tactics to Your Business Type

Prioritize the facts customers need to choose your kind of business. A local emergency service and a national online store should not use an identical content plan.

| Business type | Priority work | Useful question to answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local services | Accurate hours, service areas, qualifications, and individual service pages | “Do you offer emergency AC repair in [city], and what affects the price?” |
| Direct-to-consumer brands | Complete specifications, ingredients or materials, shipping, returns, and honest comparisons | “Is this product suitable for [specific need]?” |
| Large e-commerce stores | Current Merchant Center feeds, availability, variants, compatibility, and helpful category pages | “Which accessories fit [model]?” |
| Professional and B2B services | Clear scope, who the service suits, named expertise, case studies, and pricing factors | “What should a [business type] expect from [service]?” |

For direct-to-consumer brands, keep information accurate on the retailers customers actually use. An Amazon listing is not mandatory for every brand. Prices may legitimately differ by seller or promotion; make conditions clear rather than forcing every price to match.

For large catalogs, fix repeated data problems across the catalog instead of manually polishing a few products. For local businesses, publish location-specific facts only where you genuinely operate.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

##### Is AEO the same as SEO?

No. SEO focuses on visibility in search results; AEO focuses on being included, cited, or recommended in AI answers. They share important foundations, including accessible pages and useful content. Keep both rather than treating AEO as a replacement for SEO.

##### How long does it take to get recommended by AI?

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. Timing varies, and nobody can guarantee a recommendation.

##### Does schema markup guarantee AI citations?

No. Schema describes the information on a page in a structured format, but it does not guarantee a citation or recommendation. Use accurate markup that matches visible content, and fix access and content problems too.

##### How many reviews do I need to get recommended?

There is no proven minimum review count that guarantees an AI recommendation. Honest, relevant reviews can help people and search systems understand customer experiences. Follow each platform's review policies, and do not buy reviews or require positive ratings.

##### Can a small brand compete with a larger company in AI search?

Yes, a small brand can be relevant to a specific customer need even when larger brands dominate a broad category. Focus on clear product details, useful comparisons, and verifiable evidence. Being smaller does not prevent inclusion, but good formatting alone does not ensure it.

##### Can I pay someone to guarantee a ChatGPT recommendation?

No provider can guarantee that ChatGPT will recommend your business in a specific answer. Paying for AEO buys research, website improvements, content, and measurement—not control over the platform's response. Be cautious of promises of permanent or guaranteed placement.

It takes about two minutes, with no signup needed to run it.

## Why ChatGPT Doesn't Recommend Your Business (And How to Fix It)

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/why-chatgpt-doesnt-recommend-your-business-and-how-to-fix-it
Published: 2026-10-30
Summary: Learn why ChatGPT skips your business, why competitors get named, and what local businesses can fix. Use a five-prompt test to check your AI visibility.

ChatGPT may skip your business because it cannot find enough clear, current information connecting your name, services, location, and reputation. A competitor can appear instead because the sources retrieved for that question support that business more clearly—not necessarily because it is the better business. Strong Google rankings can help, but they do not guarantee an AI recommendation.

Someone asks, “Who are the best [your category] businesses in [your city]?” Your competitor gets named. You don't. The useful question is not whether AI dislikes your business. It is what evidence the answer used, and what was missing about you.

#### How AI assistants decide who to recommend

AI assistants can combine existing model knowledge with information retrieved from the web and other sources. When web search is used, the answer depends partly on which sources the system finds and what those sources actually support.

For a business recommendation, useful evidence includes:
- A clear business identity and accurate contact information.
- Services that match the customer's specific need.
- A location or service area that fits the request.
- Independent information about the business, such as reviews and industry coverage.
- Accessible pages that explain the relevant facts directly.

These are practical checks, not a published ranking formula. Platforms differ, and a recommendation can change with the wording, location, or timing of the question.

A mention and a citation are also different. An assistant can name your business without linking to your website. It can also cite your article as a source without recommending your business as a provider.

##### Why Google rankings don't transfer automatically

Ranking well in Google does not ensure that ChatGPT will retrieve or cite the same pages. The overlap varies by platform, question, and study method.

A [2025 Ahrefs study](https://ahrefs.com/blog/chatgpt-google-citations/) covering 3,311 short-tail keywords found 10% URL overlap and 31.8% domain overlap between ChatGPT citations and Google's top 10 results. Those figures describe that study's sample, not every search or AI platform.

The lesson is narrower—and more useful—than “SEO doesn't matter.” Search visibility still matters. But your Google rankings are not a substitute for checking actual AI answers. For the broader comparison, see [AEO vs SEO](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo).

#### Why your competitor shows up and you don't

Your competitor may have clearer evidence for the exact question being asked. Compare the sources supporting its recommendation with the information available about your business before deciding what to fix.

Five gaps are worth checking first.

##### 1. Your business identity is harder to verify

Conflicting names, old phone numbers, unclear service categories, and outdated addresses make your business harder to identify correctly. A competitor with accurate information across its website and major profiles gives customers and AI systems fewer contradictions to resolve.

Look for meaningful errors: an old location, a disconnected number, or a profile describing services you no longer offer. A harmless abbreviation such as “St.” versus “Street” is not proof of an AI penalty. Factual consistency matters more than matching every character.

##### 2. Your important pages are difficult to access

A useful page cannot support an answer if the system cannot retrieve its information. Crawl restrictions, login requirements, broken pages, or important details hidden in images can limit access.

Check whether your main service pages are publicly available and whether their essential facts appear as readable text. Robots.txt rules and security settings deserve attention, but allowing access does not guarantee indexing, retrieval, or citation.

##### 3. Independent sources say more about your competitor

A business with detailed reviews, relevant industry listings, and credible local coverage gives an assistant more material to work with. Your own claim that you are “the best” is not the same as independent evidence.

Inspect the sources actually cited in your market. They might include Yelp, BBB, Angi, a local publication, or a specialist directory. Do not assume Reddit or any other single website is the answer for every industry.

Reviews can also supply useful detail. “Fixed our burst pipe on a Sunday in North Austin” says more about service and location than “great company.” That does not establish a universal review-count threshold or a guaranteed recommendation advantage.

##### 4. Their pages answer the customer's question

A specific service explanation is more useful than a broad promotional homepage. If the question is about emergency repairs, the page should explain emergency availability, the work offered, service boundaries, and any relevant limits.

Questions about cost, timing, suitability, and comparisons are common gaps. A roofing website might describe its workmanship but never explain what an inspection includes or what affects repair costs. A competitor that answers those questions provides more usable material.

##### 5. Their claims are easier to check

Named customer examples, current licenses where required, professional credentials, and documented outcomes make claims easier to assess. Unsupported superlatives do not.

An older competitor may have accumulated more evidence over time. That is a head start, not a permanent lock on AI answers. New businesses can still provide accurate information and strong proof for a specific need.

#### Why so few local businesses get named

Local AI answers often present a shortlist rather than a long results page. Each named business must fit both the requested service and the location, which makes vague or incomplete local information especially limiting.

The demand is already there. [BrightLocal's Local Consumer Review Survey 2026](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) found that 45% of consumers used AI tools to find local business recommendations, compared with 6% a year earlier.

The supply of recommended businesses is much narrower in some research samples. The SOCi findings summarized in [BrightLocal's local SEO statistics](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/local-seo-statistics/) reported a 1.2% ChatGPT recommendation rate for sampled multi-location business locations, compared with a 35.9% average appearance rate in Google's local 3-Pack.

Those are different measures within a particular sample. They do **not** establish that 98.8% of all local businesses are invisible to every AI system. They do show why Google Maps visibility alone should not be treated as proof of ChatGPT visibility.

##### What the local winners do

Businesses that are easier to assess connect their services to real local evidence. They explain where they work, what they can handle, and what supports those claims.

Consider: “Who can fix a burst pipe in North Austin today?” A useful business page would make these facts clear:
- Whether emergency plumbing is actually offered.
- Whether North Austin is within the service area.
- How customers can confirm today's availability.
- Whether documented work or customer feedback supports that service.

A page saying “quality home services across Texas” leaves those questions unanswered. A page with accurate service details and a relevant local example gives the assistant more to use. Neither page guarantees a recommendation.

Thin city pages that only swap place names add little useful evidence. Real project details, original photos, local customer examples, and honest service boundaries are more helpful than claiming to serve every nearby city.

Your website still matters. The same BrightLocal statistics page reports that business websites account for 58% of ChatGPT Search's local search sources in the research it summarizes. That finding should not be generalized to every platform, but it is a reminder not to neglect your own pages while chasing outside mentions.

#### How to check your visibility with the five-prompt self-test

Run five prompts to separate basic business recognition from actual customer recommendations. Use ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity, and record Google AI Overviews separately if you test those too.

##### The five prompts

Each prompt checks a different part of the problem. Replace the placeholders with your business, service, category, city, and main competitor.
1. **“What do you know about [your business name]?”** Check whether the answer identifies the right business and gets its services, location, and contact details right.
2. **“Who are the best [your category] businesses in [your city]?”** Record whether you appear, which competitors appear, and what reasons or sources support the choices.
3. **“I need [your service] in [your city]. What do you recommend?”** This tests a customer need rather than simple brand recognition.
4. **“What are the pros and cons of [your business name]?”** Check the evidence behind the answer. A vague or missing answer may reflect limited retrieved information; it does not prove that no reputation information exists.
5. **“Compare [your business] with [main competitor].”** Look for factual errors, unequal detail, and unsupported claims about either business.

Run each prompt twice in fresh conversations. Keep the wording and stated location the same, and save the date, answer, and source links. Five prompts across three platforms, repeated twice, produces 30 answers—not a complete measurement program, but a useful starting point.

##### How to read the results

Treat the answers as clues to investigate, not automatic diagnoses. A business can be missing for several reasons at once.

| What you see | What to investigate |
| --- | --- |
| The answer describes the wrong business | Name ambiguity, old profiles, and unclear website identity |
| AI knows your name but never recommends you | Service fit, local relevance, and supporting evidence |
| Competitors appear with specific cited sources | Which sources support them and whether your information is missing or outdated |
| You are named but your website is not linked | A mention without a direct website citation |
| Results change between runs | Normal answer variability as well as possible information gaps |

For a quicker starting point, the [Free AI Check](https://report.audienceintent.ai/) asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI the questions your customers ask. It shows whether they name you or a competitor and lists what to fix. It takes about two minutes, with no signup needed to run it.

#### What to fix first

Fix the clearest obstacle before publishing more content. More articles will not correct a wrong business identity, an inaccessible service page, or an unsupported service-area claim.

Use this order to choose your first priority:
1. **Access and accuracy:** Can the relevant pages be read, and are your business facts correct?
2. **Service and location fit:** Do those pages explain the exact work and areas customers ask about?
3. **Evidence and useful answers:** Can a reader verify your claims and find a direct answer to the question?

Structured data can help describe your business and services when it matches visible page content. It does not create credibility by itself. There is no established rule that adding FAQ or LocalBusiness schema automatically earns a citation.

This page is the diagnosis. For the full implementation sequence, use [the step-by-step guide to getting your business recommended by ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines).

#### How to tell whether you are improving

Measure repeated answers to a consistent set of customer questions. One favorable screenshot does not establish steady visibility, and one missing mention does not establish failure.

[BrightLocal's 2026 local AI visibility study](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-ai-visibility-study/) analyzed 200,085 localized prompts. It reported that ChatGPT returned the same business lists on repeated tests only 23% of the time, with overlap falling to 4% across different declared locations.

That variability is why the question set and location need to stay consistent. Track these outcomes separately:

| Measure | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| Mentions | How often tested answers name your business |
| Website citations | How often tested answers link to your website |
| Share of voice | Your share of business mentions compared with a defined competitor set |
| AI referral traffic | Visits attributed to AI sources in your analytics |

Keep the prompt set, counting method, and competitor set consistent when comparing periods. Analytics can miss some AI-origin visits, so referral traffic is useful but incomplete.

Most importantly, separate branded questions from unbranded ones. “What do you know about Acme Plumbing?” checks recognition. “Who handles emergency pipe repairs in Austin?” checks whether AI introduces your business to someone who did not ask for you by name.

For more detail, see [how to measure AEO mentions, citations, and share of voice](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-measure-the-success-of-an-aeo-campaign-metrics-kpis-and-benchmarks-for-2026).

#### How long improvement realistically takes

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis.

Finding a page and recommending the business are different outcomes. Progress depends on your starting point, category, location, competition, and the questions being tested.

Nobody can guarantee that your business will appear in a specific AI answer. Be cautious of promises tied to a fixed ranking or an exact recommendation date. See [why nobody can guarantee the number-one answer in AI search](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/no-one-can-guarantee-youll-be-the-number-1-answer-in-ai-search-heres-what-actually-works).

#### Frequently Asked Questions

##### Why doesn't ChatGPT recommend my business?

ChatGPT may lack clear, accessible information connecting your business to the requested service and location. Inaccurate business details, limited supporting evidence, inaccessible pages, or content that does not answer the question can all contribute. A missing mention does not, by itself, prove a penalty.

##### Can I rank well on Google and still be absent from AI answers?

Yes. Strong Google rankings do not guarantee an AI recommendation. A 2025 Ahrefs study found only 10% URL overlap between ChatGPT citations and Google's top 10 results in its sample. Check AI answers directly rather than using Google rankings as a substitute.

##### Why does ChatGPT recommend my competitor instead of me?

Your competitor may have clearer service details, stronger local relevance, or more supporting information in the sources retrieved for that question. Inspect the cited evidence and repeat the test before drawing conclusions. One answer is not a stable competitive ranking.

##### Does Google Business Profile help with AI visibility?

An accurate Google Business Profile provides useful business facts, including category, location, hours, and contact details. Keep it consistent with your website and major profiles. It is one source of information, not a guarantee that ChatGPT or Google AI will recommend you.

##### Will adding schema make ChatGPT recommend my business?

No. Schema can clarify information that already appears on your pages, but it cannot replace useful content or independent evidence. Adding LocalBusiness, Service, or FAQ markup does not guarantee a mention or citation.

##### How long does it take to improve AI visibility?

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. Timing varies, and nobody can guarantee inclusion in a specific AI answer.

## How AI Search Engines Like ChatGPT Decide Which Businesses to Recommend (And How to Be One of Them)

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-ai-search-engines-like-chatgpt-decide-which-businesses-to-recommend-and-how-to-be-one-of-them
Published: 2026-09-09
Summary: AI search doesn't rank businesses. It eliminates most first, then recommends the easiest ones to verify. Learn the signals that matter.

When a potential customer types "best HVAC company in Austin" or "who's the top marketing agency in Denver" into ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google's AI Mode, they're not getting a ranked list based on star ratings. They're getting a recommendation built from whatever those systems can verify about your business at that exact moment.

Most businesses assume they're not showing up because they haven't "done AI SEO yet." The real reason is simpler and more fixable: AI assistants can't confirm enough about them from independent sources to feel confident making a recommendation. The system doesn't penalize you. It just skips you.

**The businesses that get recommended aren't necessarily the best in their category. They're the easiest to verify.**

This article breaks down exactly how AI search engines decide which businesses to name in their answers, why the selection process looks nothing like traditional search rankings, and what you can do to stop being the business that gets skipped.

> **Key stat:** AI search traffic converts at roughly 14% compared to 2.8% for traditional organic search, according to [Toolsolved's 2026 analysis](https://mentionova.com/blog/organic-traffic-decline-statistics). That's a 5x conversion advantage. The businesses getting recommended are capturing buyers who are already decided. The ones that aren't are losing those buyers to competitors.

#### AI Doesn't Rank Businesses. It Eliminates Most of Them First.

Here's the distinction every business owner needs to understand: AI search engines don't operate like Google's blue-link rankings, where every business competes for position 1 through 10. They operate through a two-step process that's closer to a background check than a competition.

**Step 1: Elimination.** The system filters out any business it cannot confidently verify. If your name, address, phone number, or service descriptions are inconsistent across directories, the AI treats that as an unresolvable conflict and removes you from consideration. Research conducted across 92 queries spanning 23 industries found that [AI platforms eliminate businesses with fragmented information before selecting who to recommend](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/07/tmt-newswire/plentisoft/how-ai-decides-which-businesses-to-recommend-new-guide-released/2419650). Inconsistency isn't a minor flaw. It's a disqualifier.

**Step 2: Selection.** From the businesses that survive the verification filter, the AI selects those with the strongest corroboration from independent sources: roundup articles, forum discussions, review platforms, and editorial mentions. Your own website plays a smaller role than most business owners expect.

##### How ChatGPT Actually Searches for Businesses

When search is enabled, ChatGPT doesn't consult a fixed leaderboard. It runs a live web search at the moment someone asks a question, reads the pages it retrieves, synthesizes an answer in natural language, and links the sources it used. According to [OpenAI's own documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8077698-how-does-chatgpt-search-work), no one can guarantee placement in those results because they change with every query.

The four-step chain looks like this:
1. **Query** — A user asks something like "best roofing contractor in Tampa." ChatGPT interprets the intent and decides to search.
2. **Retrieval** — It pulls a set of web pages relevant to that specific question. This is live, per-query, and changes over time.
3. **Synthesis** — It writes an answer in natural language from the retrieved material, not a ranked list.
4. **Citation** — It links the sources it actually used. A business can only be cited if a page containing its information was retrieved and trusted during that search.

The practical implication: if no retrieved page contains credible, consistent information about your business, you don't appear. It's not a ranking problem. It's a retrieval problem.

##### The 85% Rule

One number reshapes how most business owners think about AI visibility: roughly 85% of AI business citations come from third-party sources, not the business's own website. Only about 15% of citations point back to the business itself, per research from [Lesli.com's analysis of hundreds of AI queries](https://lesli.com/insights/ai-discoverability/how-chatgpt-recommends-businesses).

A separate study analyzing 110 customer queries across 11 US cities found that city and national editorial content supplied nearly 49% of all cited domains. Community discussions supplied another 10%. Not a single answer pulled from a Google Business Profile, Yelp, or Apple Maps page to decide which businesses to name.

**The profiles you polish aren't what AI reads. The articles and forum discussions about you are.**

This doesn't mean your website or directory listings don't matter. They matter for a different reason: consistency. But the sentence that names your business in an AI answer almost always comes from a third-party source that talks about you, not from you talking about yourself.

#### The 6 Signals AI Uses to Decide Who Gets Recommended

Once you understand the elimination-then-selection framework, the question becomes: what signals push a business from "eliminated" to "cited"? The research across multiple AI platforms points to six consistent factors.

##### 1\. Entity Clarity (The Prerequisite)

AI systems need to understand what your business is, what it does, and who it serves before they can recommend it to anyone. If your website says one thing and your Clutch profile says something different, that ambiguity works against you.

This means your business name, address, phone number, category, and service descriptions must be identical everywhere they appear online. Not similar. Identical. When an AI encounters conflicting information, it registers as an unresolvable data conflict and triggers elimination. Consistency isn't a nice-to-have. It's the price of entry.

##### 2\. Third-Party Citations and Mentions

This is the single biggest lever. Businesses appearing in at least three independent review sources are [5.7x more likely to be cited in AI-generated answers](https://www.adventyx.ai/blog/2026-04-13-how-chatgpt-recommends-brands) compared to businesses with fewer external mentions, according to research from Semrush.

The sources that carry the most weight:
- **Roundup articles and listicles** ("Best HVAC companies in Tampa," "Top marketing agencies in Denver"). Nearly 90% of third-party AI citations come from this category.
- **Reddit and forum discussions** where real users recommend your business by name. AI models treat these as authentic human opinion, which carries significant weight.
- **Industry directories and professional associations** that list your business with consistent details.
- **Wikipedia** accounts for roughly 7.8% of AI citations for established brands. Less relevant for local businesses, but worth noting for category-level context.

##### 3\. Review Quality and Recency

Reviews appeared in 77% of AI responses across a recent study of 92 queries spanning 23 industries. But the study found that quality and recency matter far more than volume. A business with 40 detailed, recent reviews consistently outperformed competitors with 200 generic five-star ratings.

What "quality" means in this context: reviews that describe the actual job done, the specific problem solved, or the experience in concrete terms. "Great service!" tells an AI nothing useful. "They replaced our entire HVAC system in one day and followed up three weeks later to make sure everything was running" gives the AI something to work with.

If your most recent review is from 2022, that's a problem regardless of how many you have. See our guide on how to ask customers for reviews in a way that actually generates useful content).

##### 4\. Content Depth on Relevant Topics

AI systems look for businesses that have demonstrated expertise in the specific area someone is asking about. A law firm with 20 detailed articles about employment law is more likely to be recommended for employment law queries than one with a generic "our services" page.

This applies to service businesses too. If someone asks "who does kitchen remodels in Phoenix," a contractor with a detailed page about kitchen remodeling in Phoenix, including specific materials used, typical timelines, and local permit considerations, has a structural advantage over one with a generic services page.

Content that answers questions directly, uses specific facts and figures, and is organized with clear headings gets extracted and cited at higher rates than long-form prose with no structure.

##### 5\. Structured Data and Crawlability

Schema markup helps AI systems understand the factual details about your business: services offered, locations, team members, pricing structures, and reviews. Businesses with comprehensive schema are easier to parse and cite accurately.

Equally important: AI crawlers need to be able to reach your site. A business that has blocked bots in its robots.txt file, or that sits behind aggressive bot-protection, is invisible to AI systems regardless of how good its content is.

##### 6\. Content Freshness

ChatGPT's real-time search component means recently published or updated content carries more weight for queries about current services, pricing, and availability. A service page last updated in 2023 will lose to a competitor's page updated last month, especially for queries about pricing or current offerings.

This doesn't mean publishing content for the sake of it. It means keeping your service pages accurate and adding content that answers the questions your customers are actually asking right now.

---
| Signal | Businesses That Get Cited | Businesses That Get Skipped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business information | Identical name, address, phone across 10+ directories | Inconsistent or outdated info across platforms |
| Third-party mentions | Referenced in roundups, forums, editorial content | No independent mentions anywhere |
| Reviews | 40+ detailed, recent reviews across multiple platforms | Few reviews, or only on one platform |
| Website content | Specific, question-answering pages for each service | Generic service page with bullet points |
| Structured data | Organization, FAQ, Service, and Review schema in place | No schema markup |
| Content freshness | Updated within the last 30 days | Website unchanged for 6+ months |

#### How ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Each Weigh These Signals Differently

The signals above apply across all major AI platforms, but each one weighs them differently. Understanding the differences matters because a strategy that works well for ChatGPT may underperform on Perplexity, and vice versa.

##### ChatGPT (with Search)

ChatGPT with search enabled runs live queries at the moment of the conversation. Its selection process is heavily influenced by recency: a page published or updated recently has a structural advantage over older content. ChatGPT also shows a notable preference for editorial sources, specifically articles that explicitly name and evaluate businesses, over raw directory listings.

One finding worth knowing: [ChatGPT users click out to external websites roughly twice as often as Google users](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-seo-statistics/), averaging 1.4 outbound links per visit versus 0.6 from Google. This means being cited in a ChatGPT response drives more actual traffic than being cited in a Google AI Overview.

##### Perplexity

Perplexity behaves more like a research assistant than a recommendation engine. It synthesizes from multiple sources simultaneously and shows its citations inline, making source transparency a core part of the experience. Businesses that appear in multiple high-authority sources benefit disproportionately here because Perplexity's synthesis model rewards corroboration. A business mentioned in five separate credible sources will appear in more Perplexity answers than one with a single strong mention.

Perplexity also indexes Reddit and forum content aggressively. Authentic community discussions about your business carry more weight on Perplexity than on any other major platform.

##### Google AI Mode and AI Overviews

Google's AI systems have access to all the signals Google has been collecting for years: your Google Business Profile, your local search rankings, your review velocity, and your website's existing authority. This gives established local businesses a potential advantage they don't have on ChatGPT or Perplexity.

But there's a catch. [When AI Overviews appear, organic click-through rates drop 58-61%](https://mentionova.com/blog/organic-traffic-decline-statistics) on those queries, per Toolsolved's 2026 analysis. Google's AI is simultaneously making it easier to be cited and harder to get traffic from traditional rankings. The businesses that benefit are the ones cited inside the AI Overview, not the ones ranking below it.

One critical data point: [only 12% of pages cited by ChatGPT rank in Google's top 10](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo)). Ranking well on Google does not translate to being recommended by AI. They are separate ecosystems with different selection criteria, and businesses that treat them as the same thing will underperform on both.

##### Claude and Gemini

Claude, built by Anthropic, relies primarily on its training data and, when search is enabled, live retrieval similar to ChatGPT. It tends to prefer authoritative, well-structured sources and is more conservative about naming specific businesses without strong corroboration. Google's Gemini integrates tightly with Google's knowledge graph, meaning your Google Business Profile and verified Google properties carry more weight here than on non-Google platforms.

The strategic takeaway: building citations across multiple independent sources is the only approach that works across all platforms simultaneously. A narrow strategy optimized for one platform creates fragility.

#### Why Most Businesses Are Invisible to AI (And Don't Know It)

Most businesses that aren't getting recommended by AI aren't doing anything wrong. They're just doing things that only worked for traditional search.

The assumption that "if I rank on Google, I'll show up in AI" is the most expensive misconception in digital marketing right now. [As we've covered in detail](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo)), AI visibility and SEO are separate ecosystems with different selection criteria. A strong Google ranking does not transfer to AI citations. The pages AI systems cite and the pages Google ranks are largely different pages.

##### The Three Most Common Reasons Businesses Get Skipped

**1\. No independent footprint.** The business exists only on its own website and maybe a Yelp page. There are no roundup articles mentioning it, no forum discussions recommending it, no editorial content that names it. AI systems have no third-party corroboration to work from. They skip it.

**2\. Inconsistent information across platforms.** The business name is slightly different on Google versus LinkedIn versus a local directory. The phone number has changed but wasn't updated everywhere. The address is formatted differently in different places. Each inconsistency is a small signal to the AI that the information may be unreliable. Enough inconsistencies and the system eliminates the business from consideration before it even gets to the selection stage.

**3\. Website content that doesn't answer questions.** Most business websites are written to describe what the business does, not to answer the questions customers are actually asking. AI systems are looking for content that matches specific queries. "We provide comprehensive HVAC solutions for residential and commercial clients" doesn't match the query "best HVAC company in Tampa." A page titled "HVAC Repair and Installation in Tampa: What to Expect, What It Costs, and Who to Call" does.

> **The visibility gap is measurable.** Research cited in our analysis of [why 98.8% of local businesses are invisible to AI](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/ai-recommended-your-competitor-not-you-heres-the-revenue-math) found that the overwhelming majority of local businesses have no meaningful presence in AI-generated answers. The businesses that do appear are not necessarily larger or better-funded. They're the ones that have built a presence on the sources AI systems actually read.

The cost of this invisibility is growing. [AI referral sessions grew 527% year over year](https://www.shadow.inc/resources/ai-search-traffic-vs-organic), according to Previsible's 2025 analysis. Those sessions convert at 14% versus 2.8% for traditional organic. Every month a business spends invisible to AI is a month of high-intent buyers going to whoever does show up.

#### What Getting Recommended by AI Actually Does for Your Business

Before getting into the mechanics of how to build AI visibility, it's worth being direct about why it matters financially. The traffic numbers are still small for most businesses. But the quality of that traffic is unlike anything traditional search has delivered.

The conversion data across multiple 2025-2026 studies tells a consistent story:
- [RankScience's analysis of 12 million website visits](https://kozec.ai/ai-sourced-traffic-conversion-rates-vs-organic-search/) found AI traffic converting at 14.2% versus organic search's 2.8%, a 5x advantage.
- [Semrush's 2025 study across 500+ B2B topics](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-seo-statistics/) found AI-referred visitors are worth 4.4x more than traditional organic visitors.
- Rocket Agency's 18-month longitudinal study found ChatGPT visits converting at 5.1x organic, the most sustained dataset available.
- Shopify's Q1 2026 figures show AI-referred sessions converting nearly 50% higher than organic search, with 14% higher average order values.

**The pattern is clear: people who find a business through an AI recommendation have already been through a research and vetting process.** The AI did the comparison work for them. By the time they arrive at your website or call your number, they're much further along in the buying decision than someone who clicked a search result.

This also explains why [Craft Food Tours saw a 312% increase in traffic from AI search within 90 days](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines) of building their AI citation presence. The traffic volume was modest compared to their Google traffic. The intent level was not.

The businesses that move first in their local market have a compounding advantage. AI systems learn from what's already being cited. The more a business gets cited, the more it gets cited. Early movers in most local categories are building a structural lead that will be difficult for later entrants to close.

#### How to Make Your Business Recommendable by AI

The mechanics are knowable. The execution takes consistent effort across multiple channels. Here's what the research shows actually moves the needle.

##### Build Your Third-Party Citation Footprint

The most important work happens off your own website. You need to appear, by name, in sources that AI systems trust. That means:
- Getting listed in industry-specific directories and roundup articles in your category
- Earning mentions in local editorial content ("best of" lists, local business features)
- Building a presence in community discussions where your category is talked about
- Ensuring your business appears consistently in review platforms beyond just Google: Yelp, BBB, Trustpilot, and industry-specific platforms depending on your category

This cannot be faked or shortcut. AI systems are trained to recognize manufactured citations. The goal is genuine, independent corroboration from sources that have no financial relationship with your business.

##### Fix Your Information Consistency

Before any citation-building work pays off, your business information needs to be identical across every platform where you appear. This is an audit, not a one-time fix. New directories appear, old ones change their data, and a phone number or address change can introduce inconsistencies across dozens of platforms simultaneously.

At minimum, audit: Google Business Profile, Yelp, Facebook, LinkedIn, your website's contact page, Apple Maps, Bing Places, and any industry directories in your category. Every field should match exactly.

##### Create Content That Answers Specific Questions

For each service you offer, create a dedicated page that answers the questions someone would ask before hiring you. Not "we offer HVAC services." Instead: what does HVAC installation cost in your city, how long does it take, what brands do you use, what warranty do you provide, and what should a customer expect on the day of service.

Structure each page with clear headings, specific numbers where you have them, and a FAQ section at the bottom. Content structured this way is extracted and cited by AI systems at significantly higher rates than unstructured prose.

For a full breakdown of what this looks like in practice, see our guide on [how to get your business recommended by AI search engines](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines).

##### Implement Schema Markup

Add structured data to your website so AI crawlers can parse your business details without ambiguity. The schema types that matter most for local businesses:
- **Organization schema**: business name, address, phone, social profiles
- **LocalBusiness schema**: hours, service area, categories
- **FAQ schema**: answers to common customer questions, formatted for direct extraction
- **Review schema**: aggregate ratings and individual review markup
- **Service schema**: descriptions of each service you offer

This is technical work that most businesses haven't done. That's an opportunity. Competitors who haven't implemented schema are easier to outrank in AI citations.

##### Track What's Actually Happening

You cannot improve what you don't measure. AI visibility requires tracking which prompts your business appears in, which platforms are citing you, and how that citation count changes over time. AudienceIntent's [Free AI Check](https://report.audienceintent.ai/) asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI the questions your customers ask. It shows whether they name you or a competitor and lists what to fix.

The Free AI Check takes about two minutes. No signup is needed to run it.

#### The Timeline: What to Expect and When

One of the most common questions business owners ask when they start working on AI visibility is how long it takes to see results. The honest answer depends on your starting point, but the pattern across businesses that have done this work is consistent.

| Timeframe | What Typically Happens |
| --- | --- |
| Days 1-30 | Information consistency is fixed, schema is implemented, foundational content is created. AI crawlers can now parse your business accurately. |
| First few weeks | Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. |
| Months 2-3 | ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why AudienceIntent starts with 90 days. |
| 90+ days | Keep content and business information current and track results. Nobody can guarantee a business will appear in a specific AI answer. |

This is not a campaign with a start and end date. AI visibility is an ongoing presence-building effort. The businesses that treat it as a one-time project tend to see initial gains followed by stagnation. The ones that maintain it consistently see compounding returns.

**What this means practically:** if your competitor started building AI citations three months ago and you haven't started yet, they have a head start that grows every week. The category leader in AI recommendations for your market will be determined in the next 12-18 months. Most categories don't have a clear winner yet.

For businesses that want to understand the full scope of what building AI visibility involves, [our complete guide to AEO strategy in 2026](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-get-your-business-recommended-by-ai-search-engines) covers the methodology in detail.

#### The Bottom Line

AI search engines don't pick the best business. They pick the most verifiable one from the sources they trust.

That's a solvable problem. It requires building a presence across the third-party sources AI systems actually read, keeping your business information consistent across every platform, creating content that answers the specific questions your customers are asking, and tracking your citation presence the same way you track any other marketing channel.

The businesses that figure this out first in their local market will have a structural advantage that compounds over time. The ones that wait until AI recommendations are obviously important will be competing against entrenched citations that took months to build.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

##### How does ChatGPT decide which businesses to recommend?

ChatGPT runs a live web search at the moment of the query, retrieves pages it considers relevant and trustworthy, synthesizes an answer in natural language, and cites the sources it used. A business gets named only if a page containing credible, consistent information about it was retrieved and trusted during that search. There is no fixed leaderboard. The results change with every query, which is why building a presence across multiple independent sources matters more than optimizing any single page.

##### Why isn't my business showing up in AI search results?

The most common reasons are: no independent footprint (the business exists only on its own website with no third-party mentions), inconsistent information across platforms (different name, address, or phone number in different directories), or website content that describes services rather than answering the specific questions customers are asking. AI systems verify businesses against third-party sources before recommending them. If those sources don't exist or conflict with each other, the business gets eliminated before the selection stage even begins.

##### Is AI visibility the same as SEO?

No. Only 12% of pages cited by ChatGPT rank in Google's top 10. They are separate ecosystems with different selection criteria. SEO optimizes for Google's ranking algorithm. AI visibility builds a presence across the third-party sources, forum discussions, editorial content, and structured data that AI systems read when deciding who to recommend. A strong Google ranking does not transfer to AI citations, and vice versa.

##### How long does it take to start showing up in AI recommendations?

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why AudienceIntent's service starts with 90 days. Nobody can guarantee a business will appear in a specific AI answer. This is not a one-time project. AI visibility compounds over time, and the gap between early movers and late entrants grows each month.

##### What is the difference between AI citations and regular backlinks?

A backlink is a hyperlink from one website to another, used primarily as a signal in Google's ranking algorithm. An AI citation is when an AI assistant names or references your business in a generated answer, with or without a clickable link. The sources that generate AI citations are often the same sources that generate backlinks (editorial articles, directory listings, review platforms), but AI systems weight them differently. They prioritize corroboration across multiple independent sources over the authority of any single link.

##### Which AI platforms should I focus on first?

The most efficient approach is building citations across all major platforms simultaneously, because the third-party sources AI systems trust overlap significantly. That said, if your customers are primarily using one platform, the platform-specific differences matter. ChatGPT rewards recency and editorial mentions. Perplexity rewards corroboration across multiple sources and indexes Reddit heavily. Google AI Mode integrates your Google Business Profile and local search authority. Claude and Gemini prefer well-structured, authoritative sources with strong corroboration.

##### How do I know if my business is currently visible to AI search?

Run the [Free AI Check](https://report.audienceintent.ai/). It asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI the questions your customers ask, shows whether they name you or a competitor, and lists what to fix. It takes about two minutes. No signup is needed to run it.
