## Do You Know the 36 Other Places AI Checks Before Recommending You?

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/do-you-know-the-36-other-places-ai-checks-before-recommending-you
Published: 2026-09-20
Summary: AI assistants trust third-party signals more than your website. See the 36 source types they check, what matters most, and where to start.

Most business owners assume AI recommendations work like Google search: build a good website, maybe keep a Google Business Profile current, and the algorithm takes care of the rest. That assumption is wrong, and it is costing businesses real customers every day.

When someone asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, or Claude to recommend a service provider, those engines do not read your homepage and decide. They cross-reference a distributed web of third-party signals: directories, review platforms, community discussions, editorial coverage, structured data feeds, and more. Your website is one input among dozens. In many cases, it is not even the most important one.

**The core problem:** A [September 2026 study analyzing 3,850 commercial prompts](https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/directories-supply-41-of-ai-citations-on-supplier-selection-prompts-new-geo-and-aeo-study-finds-1036547790) across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews found that sector directories supplied 41% of citations behind AI-generated provider recommendations, against just 18% for brand-owned pages. Your competitor with a mediocre website but strong third-party presence is getting recommended. You might not be.

This article maps where AI recommendation engines actually look, compares owned media against earned media as visibility drivers, and gives you a prioritized view of which source categories move the needle most. The goal is not to overwhelm you with a list of 36 things to fix. It is to reframe the problem so you can act on the right things first.

#### Owned Media vs. Earned Media: What AI Actually Weighs

Before mapping the source categories, it helps to understand the fundamental split in how AI engines treat content. Every signal they pull falls into one of two buckets.

**Owned media** is anything your brand controls directly: your website, your Google Business Profile, your social profiles, your blog posts. You write it, you publish it, you update it. The information is accurate (or should be), but the engine knows you wrote it about yourself.

**Earned media** is everything else: reviews customers left on Yelp, a mention in a local news article, a Reddit thread where someone recommended your business, a directory listing on Angi, an industry association membership page. You did not write it. A third party did, because of something you did or are.

##### Why Earned Media Carries More Weight

AI engines are in the business of making recommendations people trust. To do that, they need signals that cannot be easily manufactured. Owned media fails that test. Any business can write glowing copy about itself. Earned media is harder to fake at scale, which is why engines weight it more heavily when synthesizing a recommendation.

The data confirms this across multiple large studies:
- Across multiple 2026 citation studies, **82% to 85% of the sources AI engines cite** in product and recommendation answers come from third parties, not the brand's own domain.
- A [Yext Research analysis of 155.5 million AI citations](https://geoaura.world/blog/geo-for-local-businesses) in Q1 2026 found that between 69% and 85% of citations point to sources a brand can influence but does not own outright.
- In a study of 100 live "best \[category\] in \[city\]" searches through Gemini, [directory and ranking sites appeared in 78% of answers](https://acromatico.com/research/ai-recommendation-study-2026). Individual business websites appeared too, but almost always as one-off citations in the long tail, never as a top-cited source.

##### The Platform Split Makes This Worse

Here is what makes the owned vs. earned distinction especially consequential: different AI engines weight these categories differently, and the overlap between what gets cited on one platform versus another is surprisingly small.

| Engine | Primary local data source | Third-party citation share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini | Google Business Profile + Maps | ~48% of citations go to owned pages |
| ChatGPT | Bing, Foursquare, Yelp | 44.7% go to directories and review platforms |
| Perplexity | Live web + Reddit + Yelp | Community and UGC signals weighted heavily |
| Claude | Verified directories + authoritative sources | 19.5% from review platforms and social |

Source: Cheers market baseline, 356,019 citations, 28 days ending September 2, 2026; Yext Research Q1 2026.

A business optimized only for Gemini (strong Google Business Profile, well-structured website) is largely invisible to ChatGPT, which cannot see Google Reviews and pulls from Foursquare, Yelp, and Bing Places instead. Win one engine and you have done almost nothing for the others. The three major engines name the same local business just 6.5% of the time, according to the Yext 155.5 million citation panel.

**The implication is direct:** if your AI visibility strategy is "update the website and keep the GBP current," you are covering maybe 20% of the signal landscape and ignoring the 80% that decides whether a competitor gets named instead of you.

#### The Six Source Categories AI Checks (and How to Prioritize Them)

The 36 individual sources AI engines check are not equally important, and treating them as a flat list is the wrong way to approach this. Group them into six categories, understand what each category signals to the engine, and you can prioritize the work that actually changes your citation rate.

##### Category 1: Review Platforms (Highest Impact)

Reviews are not just a reputation signal. They are a verification layer. AI engines use them to separate what a business claims about itself from what customers actually experienced.

[Feefo's 2026 analysis](https://www.getfancy.ai/article-geo-platforms-2026-comparative-analysis) found that ChatGPT references reviews in 58% of responses and Perplexity in 100% of responses. In Google AI Overviews, 34.5% of answers cite at least one review platform, and the top five review platforms hold 88% of all review citations.

The bar is also higher than most businesses realize. AI platforms have been observed recommending only businesses averaging 4.3 stars or higher on ChatGPT, 4.1 stars on Perplexity, and 3.9 stars on Gemini. Google Maps will still surface a business at 3.5 stars. AI will not.

**Key review platforms by engine:**
- **ChatGPT:** Yelp, TripAdvisor, Foursquare reviews (cannot access Google Reviews)
- **Gemini:** Google Reviews (primary), Trustpilot
- **Perplexity:** Yelp, Google Reviews, industry-specific platforms (Healthgrades, Avvo, Angi)
- **Claude:** BBB, high-trust industry directories, verified review platforms

The practical priority: volume and recency of reviews on Yelp and Google matter most across the broadest set of engines. If your Yelp profile has 12 reviews from 2021, that is a problem for ChatGPT visibility specifically.

##### Category 2: Directories and Listing Platforms (High Impact)

This is the category most businesses underestimate. Directories are not just for SEO anymore. They are the primary citation source for AI on supplier-selection queries.

The September 2026 Citations.press study found that directories with consistent, structured data (one entity per entry, complete attributes) were cited 3.1 times more often than directories with free-text listings. Coverage depth within a stated category was a stronger predictor of citation than domain authority.

The most cited directory and listing platforms across AI engines in the U.S.:

| Platform | Primary engine benefit | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google Business Profile | Gemini, Google AI Overviews | Direct data feed to Google's AI layer |
| Yelp | ChatGPT, Perplexity | ChatGPT's primary local data source |
| Bing Places | ChatGPT | ChatGPT runs on the Bing index |
| Foursquare | ChatGPT | OpenAI licensed the Foursquare Places dataset |
| Apple Business Connect | Siri, Apple Intelligence | Separate AI ecosystem, often overlooked |
| BBB | Claude, Perplexity | High-trust verification signal |
| Angi / HomeAdvisor | ChatGPT, Perplexity | Heavily cited in home services queries |
| Industry-specific directories | All engines | Vertical relevance is a strong predictor |

Consistency across these platforms is not optional. ChatGPT's local data accuracy is only about 68%, meaning a third of what it says about your business can be wrong if your listings are stale or inconsistent. An incorrect phone number on Foursquare or an outdated address on Bing Places does not just inconvenience customers; it reduces your citation eligibility.

##### Category 3: Community Discussions and UGC (Medium-High Impact)

Reddit is the most cited single domain across AI platforms, appearing in roughly 40% of LLM citations across all major engines, according to an aggregated index of 680 million citations harvested from ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude between August 2024 and April 2026.

For Perplexity specifically, Reddit accounts for 46.7% of top sources. This is not a quirk. Perplexity is the only major engine that actively trusts user-generated content, including Facebook community groups and Nextdoor alongside Reddit.

**What this means in practice:** if customers in your city are discussing your category on Reddit and your business is not mentioned, or worse, a competitor is mentioned positively, that shapes Perplexity's recommendations. You cannot post fake Reddit threads (the platform's detection is good and AI engines are increasingly sensitive to manufactured UGC), but you can earn genuine mentions by being genuinely good and by being findable in the communities where your customers already talk.

Other community sources that factor in: Quora threads, Nextdoor business recommendations, Facebook Groups, and niche forums specific to your industry.

##### Category 4: Editorial and Publisher Coverage (Medium Impact)

When an AI engine wants to corroborate a recommendation, it looks for third-party editorial coverage: news articles, "best of" lists, industry publications, and ranked guides. Forbes, for example, appeared in 11 of 100 answers in the Gemini recommendation study. Healthgrades appeared in 9.

This category is harder to earn quickly, but it compounds. A mention in a credible local news outlet, a spot on a "best \[category\] in \[city\]" list from a regional publication, or coverage in an industry trade journal all serve as corroborating signals that the engine can cite alongside directory data.

The key distinction: these are not links for SEO. They are entity mentions that confirm your business exists, operates in a specific category, and has been recognized by a credible third party. The engine does not need to rank the article. It needs to find the mention.

##### Category 5: Structured Data and Knowledge Graph Signals (Medium Impact)

AI engines build entity models of businesses: a structured understanding of who you are, what you do, where you operate, and how you relate to other entities. Structured data on your website (LocalBusiness schema, FAQ schema, service-area markup) feeds this model directly.

Wikipedia and Wikidata play a role here for larger or more established businesses. ChatGPT cites Wikipedia in 2.49% of all its responses and it is the single most-cited domain in ChatGPT's top-ten sources. For most local businesses, Wikipedia is not accessible, but Wikidata entity records and structured schema on your own site serve a similar function at a smaller scale.

**Structured data priorities:**
- LocalBusiness schema with accurate NAP (name, address, phone), categories, hours, and service area
- FAQ schema on service pages (maps to how customers phrase AI queries)
- Review schema to surface aggregate ratings
- Breadcrumb and sitelinks schema for entity clarity

##### Category 6: Social Profiles and Brand Mentions (Lower Impact, Still Real)

Social profiles are the weakest signal category for AI recommendations, but they are not irrelevant. Claude draws 19.5% of its citations from review platforms and social profiles, roughly 7.5 times OpenAI's rate of about 2.6%. If Claude is part of your target audience's AI behavior, social presence matters more than it does for ChatGPT optimization.

The more important signal in this category is brand mention consistency: your business name appearing in the same form across LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube, matching what appears in your directory listings. Inconsistency across these profiles creates entity confusion for the engine, which reduces confidence in recommending you.

#### Where Most Businesses Are Actually Spending Their Time

The gap between where businesses invest their visibility effort and where AI engines actually look is the central problem. Most businesses concentrate almost entirely on owned media: website updates, social posts, maybe a Google Business Profile refresh. That work is not wasted, but it addresses a fraction of the signal landscape.

Here is a rough breakdown of where AI citation weight actually falls across the source categories, based on the 2026 studies cited above:

The takeaway here is not that your website does not matter. It does, especially for Gemini, which sends nearly 60% of its local citations to business websites. The takeaway is that your website alone cannot carry your AI visibility, and for ChatGPT, which handles roughly 78% of local AI query volume, third-party sources are doing more of the work than your own pages.

**The effort-to-impact mismatch looks like this:**

Most businesses spend roughly 80% of their digital marketing effort on owned media (website, social, content) and 20% or less on earned media (reviews, directories, press). AI recommendation engines weight those categories in roughly the opposite proportion. That inversion is why businesses with strong traditional SEO can still be invisible in AI search.

The fix is not to abandon your website. It is to build the earned media layer that AI engines are actually checking.

#### A Prioritization Map: Where to Start

Not every business needs to be on every platform. The right starting point depends on your category, your primary AI engine exposure, and how much of the baseline is already in place. That said, the research points to a clear sequence for most businesses.

##### Tier 1: Fix Before Anything Else

These are the signals that, if wrong or missing, actively disqualify you from AI recommendations regardless of what else you do.
- **Review rating below 4.0 on major platforms.** This is close to a hard floor for AI recommendation eligibility, not a ranking nudge. Address it before building out listings.
- **Inconsistent NAP data across platforms.** Name, address, and phone number must match exactly across Google, Yelp, Bing, Foursquare, and any directory you appear in. Inconsistency creates entity confusion.
- **Unclaimed or stale listings on Yelp, Bing Places, and Foursquare.** These three feed ChatGPT directly. A stale listing is worse than no listing because it can contain wrong information that gets cited.

##### Tier 2: Build the Core Earned Media Stack

Once the baseline is clean, build presence in the platforms with the highest citation frequency across the broadest set of engines.
1. **Google Business Profile** (complete, with photos, services, posts, and active review responses)
2. **Yelp** (claimed, complete, actively soliciting reviews)
3. **Bing Places** (claimed and synced with your GBP data)
4. **Foursquare** (claimed, complete, consistent with other listings)
5. **Apple Business Connect** (overlooked by most businesses, feeds Siri and Apple Maps AI)
6. **BBB accreditation** (high-trust signal for Claude and Perplexity)
7. **Your top 2-3 vertical directories** (Angi for home services, Healthgrades for healthcare, Avvo for legal, etc.)

##### Tier 3: Earn the Harder Signals

These take longer but compound over time and are harder for competitors to replicate quickly.
- **Community presence:** Genuine mentions in Reddit threads, Nextdoor recommendations, and local Facebook Groups. These cannot be manufactured, but they can be earned by being active and excellent in your market.
- **Editorial coverage:** A spot on a credible "best of" list, a local news mention, or a trade publication feature. Pitch these proactively; they do not happen by accident.
- **Content that answers real questions:** Pages on your site that directly answer the questions your customers ask AI assistants, structured with FAQ schema, are cited at higher rates than generic service pages.

> **The compounding effect matters.** [Rankability's 2026 citation study](https://www.rankability.com/blog/ai-search-statistics/) found that pages cited across eight or more queries had a 43.3% top-10 AI citation rate, compared to 15.5% for pages cited only once. Presence across multiple source categories can build on itself: the more places you appear, the more likely AI engines are to cite you, which increases the probability of appearing in future answers.

##### What Not to Do

A few common mistakes that waste time or actively hurt AI visibility:
- **Optimizing only for Google.** Google's AI ecosystem (Gemini, AI Overviews) and ChatGPT pull from almost entirely different source sets. Ranking well in Google Search does not transfer to ChatGPT recommendations.
- **Chasing domain authority for directories.** The September 2026 study found a weak correlation (Spearman rank of 0.19) between a directory's domain authority and how often it was cited. Coverage depth within a stated category was the stronger predictor. Being listed thoroughly in a niche directory beats a thin listing on a high-DA general one.
- **Treating AI visibility as a one-time project.** Roughly 75% to 88% of the sources AI cites change day to day. Platforms update, engines reweight sources, and new directories gain traction. This requires ongoing monitoring, not a single audit.

#### The Real Question Is What You Do Next

AI recommendation engines are not reading your website and making a judgment call. They are running a verification process across dozens of third-party sources, and the businesses that show up consistently across that ecosystem are the ones getting recommended.

Your website is not the problem. The gap in your earned media footprint is.

The first step is knowing where you actually stand. Most businesses have no idea how they appear across the source categories that matter, which listings are stale, which review platforms are dragging down their citation eligibility, or which AI engines are currently recommending a competitor instead of them.

**Run the [Free AI Check](https://report.audienceintent.ai/).** It asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI the questions your customers ask, shows whether they name you or a competitor, and lists what to fix. Takes about two minutes. No signup needed to run it.

The businesses that move on this now are building a citation footprint that compounds. The ones that wait are watching competitors get recommended in their place.

#### All 36 Sources: A Complete Reference by Category

Use this as a working checklist. The six categories match the prioritization framework above. Start with Tier 1 fixes before working down the list.

##### Category 1: Review Platforms
1. Google Reviews

## How to Find an Answer Engine Optimization Partner in 2026

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-find-an-answer-engine-optimization-agency-in-2026
Published: 2026-11-03
Summary: Learn how to choose an answer engine optimization partner that helps your business appear in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and other AI search results.

Most businesses still choose the wrong company for this work.

Not because they are careless. Because the market is noisy.

Every week, more SEO companies add "AEO" to a service page. Some are learning fast and doing solid work. Plenty are just relabeling the same old deliverables and hoping you do not know the difference.

That matters because the way people search has changed. ChatGPT can use web search and location signals for local recommendations. Google says AI Overviews now has more than 2.5 billion monthly active users, while AI Mode has passed 1 billion monthly users. OpenAI has also expanded shopping, comparison, and local search experiences, which means more buying decisions now start inside answer engines, not just in Google’s old blue links.

If your business is missing from those recommendations, strong Google rankings alone will not save you.

This guide is built for buyers. It will help you tell the difference between a company that actually knows how to improve visibility in ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity, and one that has simply updated its pitch deck. You will learn what to look for, what to ask, what results should look like in the first 90 days, and which red flags should make you walk away.

#### What an Answer Engine Optimization Partner Should Actually Do

An answer engine optimization partner helps your business appear more often when people ask ChatGPT, Google AI, or Perplexity who to choose, what to buy, or which local company looks best.

That sounds simple. It is not.

This work is not just "SEO for AI." A serious company should be improving three things at once:
- **Your visibility inside answer engines** - where your brand gets mentioned and how often
- **Your citation footprint** - which pages and third-party sources answer engines rely on when they talk about your business
- **Your trust signals** - the consistency, authority, and freshness of the information these systems can find

A weak partner will treat this like a content retainer. A strong one will treat it like a visibility system.

##### The job is bigger than writing articles

If the proposal is mostly blog posts, be careful.

Content matters, but content alone is not enough. The company you hire should be able to explain how it handles:
- Prompt tracking across ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity
- Page-level citation analysis
- Competitor comparisons
- On-site content improvements
- Crawlability and structured data issues
- Third-party profiles, reviews, and source consistency
- Reporting tied to prompts, mentions, citations, and revenue signals

If a partner cannot explain the full stack, they are probably selling a narrow slice of the job.

#### Why This Matters More in 2026

This is no longer a niche channel.

Google has publicly said AI Overviews now reaches more than 2.5 billion monthly active users, and AI Mode has surpassed 1 billion monthly users. OpenAI has expanded ChatGPT search, location-aware recommendations, and richer shopping comparisons. More people are asking a question and choosing from the answer they get back.

That changes buyer behavior in two important ways:
1. **More decisions happen before a click.** People can compare options, narrow vendors, and form opinions inside the answer itself.
2. **The winner is not always the top Google result.** Answer engines pull from multiple sources and often summarize across them.

> **What this means for buyers:** You are not hiring a company to "rank a page." You are hiring one to increase the odds that your business is recommended when someone asks who to choose.

#### How to Tell if You Need Help Now

Not every company needs outside help this minute. But most businesses can answer this pretty quickly.

You probably need help now if any of these are true:
- You rank well in Google, but your business rarely appears in ChatGPT, Google AI, or Perplexity answers
- Competitors are getting named in recommendation prompts and you are not
- You do not know which prompts mention your business today
- You cannot tell which pages or third-party sources answer engines trust in your category
- Your reviews, directory listings, or business information are inconsistent across the web
- Nobody on your team owns this work, and it keeps getting pushed behind SEO, ads, and everything else

The biggest mistake here is waiting until a competitor becomes the default recommendation.

Once an answer engine keeps seeing the same names, same sources, and same evidence, that lead compounds.

#### What to Look For in an AEO Company

This is where most buyers get misled.

A polished deck is easy. Useful reporting is harder. Real methodology is harder still.

Here is what a capable partner should be able to show you.

##### 1\. Multi-platform tracking

If they only talk about one platform, the picture is incomplete.

ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity do not behave the same way. A company worth hiring should show prompt tracking across multiple platforms and explain the differences between them.

##### 2\. Mentions and citations tracked separately

These are not the same thing.

A mention means your business name appears in an answer. A citation means the answer engine relied on a source tied to your business or linked to a page it trusted.

Both matter. But if a company lumps them together, the reporting will sound better than it is.

##### 3\. Page-level visibility, not just domain-level claims

"Your site is showing up more" is vague.

You want to know which specific pages are being cited, which are ignored, and which need rewriting. That is how the work becomes actionable instead of decorative.

##### 4\. Third-party source work

Answer engines do not build opinions from your website alone.

They also look at review platforms, business listings, publisher coverage, expert commentary, and other external signals. If a company only works on your site and ignores the rest of the web, they are leaving a large part of the job untouched.

##### 5\. A clear 90-day plan

Good partners do not promise miracles in 30 days.

They should be able to explain what happens in month one, what gets improved in months two and three, and what early wins actually look like.

A realistic first 90 days usually includes:
- Baseline prompt tracking
- Competitor benchmarking
- Fixing crawl and access issues
- Reworking key service pages
- Publishing targeted answer content
- Improving third-party trust signals
- Reporting changes by prompt and platform

##### 6\. Proof with real numbers

You do not need a hundred case studies. You do need evidence.

That means before-and-after visibility data, citation growth, prompt coverage improvements, traffic from answer engines, or business outcomes tied to the work.

Not adjectives. Numbers.

#### Red Flags That Should Make You Walk

A few warning signs usually tell the story fast.

Walk away if the partner:
- Guarantees placement in ChatGPT or Google AI
- Cannot show your current visibility before you sign
- Talks only about blog output and nothing about measurement
- Avoids competitor comparisons
- Reports vanity metrics without prompt-level detail
- Cannot explain how third-party sources affect recommendations
- Uses vague language like "we optimize for AI" without showing how
- Treats this as a one-time setup instead of ongoing visibility work

The biggest red flag is certainty.

Any partner who promises fixed placement in a system they do not control is either overselling or guessing.

#### Questions to Ask Before You Hire Anyone

Ask these before you sign anything.
1. **Which answer engines do you track today, and how often?**
2. **Can you show me where my business appears right now, and where it does not?**
3. **Do you track mentions and citations separately?**
4. **Can you show which pages are being cited and which need work?**
5. **How do you compare my visibility against competitors?**
6. **What do you do beyond writing content?**
7. **How do you handle third-party sources, reviews, and listings?**
8. **What should I realistically expect in the first 90 days?**
9. **How do you report progress each week or month?**
10. **What happens after the first 90 days?**

If a partner's answers are fuzzy, the work probably will be too.

#### What Good Reporting Should Look Like

If you are paying for this, you should not have to guess whether it is working.

A useful reporting setup should include:
- Prompt-level tracking
- Mentions by platform
- Citations by page
- Competitor share of voice
- Change over time
- Notes on what changed and why
- A short, clear summary of what matters next

That last one matters more than people think.

Business owners do not need a dashboard full of confetti. They need to know what improved, what did not, and what gets done next.

#### What Results Should Look Like in the First 90 Days

Here is the honest answer.

Nobody credible can promise that your business will suddenly be recommended everywhere in a month.

But a good partner should be able to create visible movement.

In the first 30 days, you should expect a baseline, prompt map, competitor snapshot, and a clear list of technical, content, and source issues.

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why AudienceIntent starts with 90 days.

By 90 days, you should have a clear report of the work completed and how mentions and citations have changed. Nobody can guarantee your business will appear in a specific AI answer. AudienceIntent promises the work, done properly every month, and an honest report.

#### How AudienceIntent Approaches This Work

Most companies make this too complicated.

We track where your business shows up when people ask ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity who to choose. Then we work on the pages, sources, and trust signals that influence those recommendations.

The work starts with a baseline across prompts and competitors. From there, we focus on the gaps that matter most first.

That usually means:
- Fixing what answer engines can or cannot access
- Tightening key service and location pages

And we show the numbers.

One example: Craft Food Tours saw a **312% increase in traffic from AI in 90 days**. Vault Metal went from **169 to 7,808 mentions** and **3 to 751 citations in 90 days**.

That does not mean every business gets the same result.

It does mean this work can be measured, and it should be.

#### Final Checklist

Before you hire anyone, make sure they can say yes to most of this:
- They track ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity
- They show your baseline before you sign
- They separate mentions from citations
- They compare you against competitors
- They identify which pages matter most
- They work on third-party trust signals, not just your website
- They report at prompt level
- They can show real before-and-after results
- They give you a realistic 90-day roadmap
- They do not promise what nobody can guarantee

If a partner cannot do those things, keep looking.

An answer engine optimization partner helps businesses improve how often they are mentioned or cited when people ask platforms like ChatGPT, Google AI, and Perplexity for recommendations or answers.

##### Is AEO different from SEO?

Yes. Traditional SEO focuses on ranking pages in search results. AEO focuses on whether your business gets pulled into generated answers and recommendations.

Yes. Strong Google rankings help, but they do not guarantee visibility in ChatGPT, Google AI, or Perplexity.

## How to Measure the Success of an AEO Campaign: Metrics, KPIs, and Benchmarks for 2026

URL: https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-to-measure-the-success-of-an-aeo-campaign-metrics-kpis-and-benchmarks-for-2026
Published: 2026-09-13
Summary: Measure AEO success with clear KPIs, useful benchmarks, and a weekly method for tracking AI mentions, citations, share of voice, traffic, and sales.

Measure AEO success by tracking mentions, citations, recommendations, and share of voice across a fixed set of customer questions. Repeat the same tests each week, then connect visibility changes to website visits, leads, and sales. Use your starting point and the same competitors as benchmarks—not a universal score that claims to fit every business.

#### What Does AEO Success Look Like?

A successful answer engine optimization campaign improves how often AI includes your business, how accurately it describes you, and whether that exposure brings customers. No single metric proves all three.

Use four measurement layers, with answer quality checked throughout:

| Layer | Main question | Useful measures | Data source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visibility | Does AI include or recommend us? | Mention rate, citation rate, recommendation rate, share of voice | Saved AI answers |
| Traffic | Do people visit our website? | Identifiable AI referral sessions and engagement | GA4 |
| Demand | Are more people looking for us by name? | Branded impressions, clicks, and self-reported discovery | Search Console and customer forms |
| Revenue | Do those visitors become customers? | Qualified leads, completed sales, attributed revenue | Analytics and CRM |

Check description accuracy, recommendation context, and cited URLs alongside these measures. More appearances are not necessarily better if AI gives customers the wrong service area or outdated prices.

SEO rankings remain useful, but they do not measure inclusion in AI answers. For the distinction, see [AEO vs SEO](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/aeo-vs-seo).

#### Define Your KPIs Before Counting Results

A mention, citation, and recommendation are different events. Record them separately so a rising total does not hide a weak result.

For the formulas below, one **test run** means one prompt submitted to one AI surface once. Repeating that prompt creates another observation.

##### Mention Rate

Mention rate measures the share of completed test runs whose answers name your business.

**Mention rate = runs naming your business ÷ completed test runs × 100**

Count your business once per answer, even if its name appears several times. This measures frequency of inclusion rather than repeated wording.

##### Citation Rate

Citation rate measures how often an answer links to a page on your website as a source. A citation can appear without an explicit recommendation—or even without your brand name in the answer text.

**Website citation rate = runs citing your website ÷ completed test runs × 100**

Record the exact URL. Also record third-party pages used to support statements about your business, but keep those separate from links to your own website.

For a rate, count each qualifying answer once. Track total citation links and distinct cited URLs separately; neither is interchangeable with citation rate.

##### Recommendation Rate

Recommendation rate measures how often AI presents your business as a suitable choice for the customer's need.

**Recommendation rate = runs explicitly recommending your business ÷ completed test runs × 100**

A company named in a warning or background explanation is not a recommendation. Decide what qualifies before testing, then apply that rule consistently.

##### AI Share of Voice

AI share of voice measures your share of appearances among a fixed group of businesses answering the same questions.

**Mention-based share of voice = your brand-answer appearances ÷ all tracked brands' brand-answer appearances × 100**

Count each tracked brand once per answer. If several competitors appear together, each gets one appearance.

Keep the prompt set, competitor list, and platform mix stable. Report citation-based or recommendation-based share of voice separately if useful; do not combine them using unexplained weights.

Share of voice is relative to the businesses and questions you selected. It is not market share, and a high percentage does not make you the default recommendation across all AI searches.

##### Answer Quality and Accuracy

Quality checks show whether AI is presenting your business correctly and in a useful context.

Record:
- **Placement:** first business named, later mention, or numbered-list position.
- **Recommendation context:** suitable choice, alternative, background reference, or warning.
- **Sentiment:** positive, neutral, or negative.
- **Description accuracy:** correct, partly correct, or incorrect.
- **Link accuracy:** whether the citation opens the right page and supports the claim.

Check services, location, pricing, and contact details. Keep sentiment separate from accuracy: an enthusiastic answer can still be wrong.

A composite visibility score can summarize progress, but its meaning depends on the provider's formula. Do not compare different providers' scores as though they use the same scale. See [what AudienceIntent's weekly report measures](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-audienceintent-measures-ai-visibility-every-metric-score-and-attribution-model-explained) for our reporting details.

#### Which AEO Benchmarks Are Useful in 2026?

The most useful benchmarks are your own baseline and matched competitor results. There is no reliable universal percentage that makes every business competitive across every prompt set and platform.

A small local business, national retailer, and specialist manufacturer face different questions and competitors. Branded prompts also produce different results from open questions such as “Who should I hire?”

Use this comparison framework:

| Metric | Useful benchmark | What improvement means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mention rate | Your starting rate on unchanged prompts | More tested answers include you |
| Website citation rate | Your baseline and competitors' rates | More answers link to your website |
| Recommendation rate | Results on relevant buying questions | More answers present you as a suitable choice |
| Share of voice | The same tracked competitors | Your relative presence is growing |
| Description accuracy | Verified business facts | Fewer incorrect or outdated claims |
| AI referral sessions | Comparable periods, allowing for seasonality | More identifiable visits from AI sources |
| Sales and revenue | Your own completed customer records | More observed business outcomes |

Conductor reports that [AI-referred traffic currently accounts for about 1.08% of total web visits across industries](https://www.conductor.com/academy/aeo-geo-benchmarks-report/). Its report also attributes 87.4% of measured AI referral traffic to ChatGPT. These figures describe its dataset, not targets for your business or a complete count of AI-influenced visits.

##### Use Client Results as Examples, Not Forecasts

Published results show what happened for a particular client over a stated period. They do not establish a minimum outcome for another business.

| Client | Reported result | Period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vault Metal | AI mentions 169 → 7,808 (+4,520%) and citations 3 → 751 | 90 days |
| GoldenCrest Metals | Visibility score +202.4% | 90 days |
| Craft Food Tours | Traffic from AI +312% | 90 days |

Read the [Vault Metal case study](https://www.audienceintent.ai/insights/how-vault-metal-went-from-invisible-in-ai-to-7-808-mentions-in-90-days) for that example. Before comparing any result with yours, check the prompts, platforms, observation volume, and metric definitions.

#### A Repeatable Weekly AEO Tracking Method

Reliable tracking comes from asking the same questions under comparable conditions and saving the evidence. A spreadsheet is enough to begin.

##### Step 1: Build a Small, Useful Prompt Library

Start with 15 to 25 questions based on actual customer conversations. Include discovery, comparison, and purchase questions—not just prompts that already contain your name.

| Prompt type | Example | What it tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category recommendation | “Which roofing companies serve Miami?” | Whether AI includes you without being prompted by name |
| Problem | “Who can repair a leaking flat roof in Miami?” | Whether AI connects you with a specific need |
| Selection | “What should I check before hiring a roofer?” | Whether your information helps answer buying questions |
| Comparison | “How does [business] compare with [competitor]?” | How AI describes differences |
| Brand verification | “Does [business] handle commercial roofs?” | Whether business facts are correct |

Include location and customer constraints when they matter. Keep branded and non-branded results separate so easy brand-verification questions do not inflate discovery performance.

Choose about 10 high-priority questions for weekly checks. Test the full library monthly, keeping those two datasets separate.

##### Step 2: Keep Testing Conditions Consistent

Test ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Google AI Mode. Treat Overviews and AI Mode as separate surfaces within Google AI because their answers and availability can differ.

Record the date, country or location, account state, search mode, and model label when available. Start fresh conversations rather than letting earlier messages influence the answer.

Private browsing can reduce some account effects. It does not remove location, product experiments, or all personalization.

A completed Google search with no AI Overview is a valid “no appearance” observation for an Overview exposure metric. Record it explicitly and report how often Overviews appeared. Exclude technical failures, such as an unavailable page, rather than counting them as business absences.

##### Step 3: Repeat Important Prompts and Save Answers

Repeat priority prompts three times when practical. Report the appearance frequency across those runs rather than treating one favorable answer as a stable result.

AI answers vary. Repetition helps distinguish a recurring pattern from an isolated response, but it does not produce a universal answer that every customer will see.

Save answer text, screenshots, and citation URLs. If using a tracking tool, ask whether it collects browser-visible answers, API responses, or both. Those are different observation methods; do not mix them without labeling the change.

##### Step 4: Log the Same Fields Every Time

Use one spreadsheet row per test run. A practical column set is:

`Date | Prompt ID | Prompt text | Platform/surface | Run number | Brand mentioned | Website cited | Citation URLs | Recommended | Placement | Competitors | Sentiment | Accuracy | Evidence link | Run status`

This structure lets you calculate rates without losing the underlying evidence. Record unexpected competitors too, but keep your benchmark competitor group fixed until a scheduled review.

##### Step 5: Review the Results and Choose an Action

Compare the same weekly prompt subset, not this week's short check against last month's full library.

During the review:
1. Calculate mention, citation, and recommendation rates by platform.
2. Calculate share of voice against the fixed competitor group.
3. Check inaccurate answers and broken or misleading citations.
4. Compare this week with a rolling four-week view.
5. Review AI referral sessions, leads, and sales.
6. Select one or two fixes and record what changed.

Allow separate time for collecting answers; the review itself can be brief. Keep a change log for technical fixes, revised pages, new content, and known testing changes.

##### Step 6: Refresh Without Losing Comparability

Review the full prompt library monthly and its relevance quarterly. Preserve a stable core so you can still measure long-term progress.

Add new questions and competitors as a new comparison group, or clearly mark a new baseline. Otherwise, an apparent performance change may simply reflect a harder prompt set.

#### Connect Visibility to Traffic and Demand

Use analytics to measure identifiable visits, then treat branded search and customer feedback as supporting evidence. Referral data cannot capture every person influenced by an AI answer.

##### Track AI Referrals in GA4

Create a saved report or custom channel group for identifiable AI referral sources. Start by inspecting session sources such as:
- `chatgpt.com`
- `chat.openai.com`
- `perplexity.ai`

Check the source values actually recorded in your property before writing grouping rules. Keep the rules consistent across reporting periods.

Track sessions, engaged sessions, key events, and completed sales where available. Compare conversion rates with your own other channels, and show the underlying counts when traffic is small.

Google AI Overviews and AI Mode visits may appear within Google organic traffic rather than a clean, separate AI referral source. Do not label all Google organic visits as AI traffic or assume GA4 can fully separate them.

##### Monitor Branded Search Without Claiming Causation

Track searches for your business name and common variations in Google Search Console. Compare impressions and clicks with your AI visibility trend over comparable periods.

An increase may support the wider picture, but it does not prove AI caused it. Advertising, referrals, seasonality, and other activity can also increase branded searches.

Add “How did you hear about us?” to an inquiry form or customer conversation, with an AI option. Keep self-reported discovery separate from tracked referral data so the same customer is not counted twice.

#### Connect AEO to Revenue: One Attribution Example

The strongest revenue measure is completed sales connected to identifiable visits or customer-reported discovery. A calculation based on an assumed industry conversion rate is a forecast, not measured revenue.

Use three reporting categories:
- **Session-attributed:** a recorded AI referral is connected to a purchase or lead.
- **Self-reported:** the customer says an AI answer helped them find you.
- **Possible influence:** direct traffic or branded demand rose alongside visibility, without a confirmed customer connection.

Deduplicate customers across categories. Do not present possible influence as confirmed revenue.

##### Worked Example

Suppose a business records 100 identifiable AI referral sessions in a month. Five of those sessions produce completed sales, with an average sale value of $2,000.

Its observed purchase conversion rate is 5%. The session-attributed revenue calculation is:

**100 sessions × 5% observed purchase conversion rate × $2,000 average sale value = $10,000**

This is hypothetical. It illustrates session-attributed revenue, not proof that every purchase was caused solely by AI. It also excludes untracked visits and later purchases that cannot be linked reliably.

For a business that sells through consultations, follow leads through to completed sales in the CRM. Do not multiply inquiries by average sale value as though every inquiry becomes a customer. Allow for the normal sales cycle when reviewing results.

#### Turn Tracking Gaps Into Specific Fixes

Use each gap as a diagnostic starting point, not a certain explanation. A low rate can have several causes.

| Pattern | What to investigate | Practical next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low mentions and citations | Missing answers, unclear services, crawl or indexing problems | Check access and improve pages answering the missed questions |
| Mentions without website citations | Answer format, missing supporting detail, or reliance on other sources | Inspect cited sources and make relevant website pages clearer and more useful |
| Citations without recommendations | Informational relevance but unclear fit for the buyer | Explain who the service suits, its limits, and supporting evidence |
| Incorrect descriptions | Outdated website or third-party information | Correct the facts where they appear |
| Rising visibility but flat visits | Answers may satisfy the question without a click | Check links, buying intent, and customer-reported discovery |
| Visits without sales | Poor page fit, confusing next steps, or tracking gaps | Review the landing page and conversion process |

[According to Google's guidance on helpful content](https://blog.google/products/search/google-search-helpful-content-update/), content should be made to help people. Use that principle when improving pages; it is not a promise of AI inclusion.

If visibility drops suddenly, first rerun the same prompts under the same conditions. Then check website availability, crawler access, changed citation sources, and competitor gains. Avoid assuming that a single decline proves a technical fault or negative coverage.

#### Set a Realistic Review Timeline

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why AudienceIntent's service starts with 90 days.

These are expectations, not deadlines or guarantees. Review leading indicators weekly, while allowing enough time for recommendations and customer outcomes to develop.

Its reporting tracks ChatGPT, Google AI—including AI Overviews and AI Mode—and Perplexity, with 50 prompts tracked daily, a weekly visibility report, and tracking for up to five competitors. A monthly progress call and shared Slack channel support the work.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

##### Which AEO KPIs should I track first?

Start with mention rate, website citation rate, recommendation rate, and share of voice on a fixed prompt set. Add identifiable AI referral sessions and completed customer outcomes so visibility is not mistaken for sales.

##### What is the difference between an AI mention and a citation?

A mention names your business in the answer text. A citation links to a source page. Track links to your website separately from third-party sources discussing your business; neither automatically means AI recommended you.

##### What is a good AI share of voice?

There is no universal good percentage. Compare your share with a fixed group of competitors across the same prompts and platforms. Improvement is meaningful only when the test conditions and counting method remain comparable.

##### Can I measure AEO without a paid tracking tool?

Yes. Start with 15 to 25 customer questions, check a stable priority subset weekly, and save answers in a spreadsheet. Use GA4 for identifiable referrals and Search Console for branded search trends. Repeated testing takes time, but specialist software is not required to establish a baseline.

##### How long does it take to see AEO results?

Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. ChatGPT and Google AI usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. Results vary, and nobody can guarantee inclusion in a specific answer.

##### Why are AI mentions increasing but website visits are not?

Some answers name businesses without linking, and some users act without visiting the website. Other users search for the brand later. Check citation links and prompt intent before concluding that the campaign has failed or that a technical problem exists.

##### Can I measure all revenue influenced by AI?

Not exactly. Referral data misses some visits, and later branded searches or direct visits may have several causes. Report session-attributed revenue, self-reported AI discovery, and possible influence separately, while counting each customer only once.
